# Defiant — Medical Tourism in Chiang Mai, Pay Local Prices
URL: https://defiant.to/

# DEFIANT

## World-class care in Thailand. Pay what the locals pay.

Get the treatment you need in Chiang Mai for **50–80% less than the US** — surgery,
dental, HRT, senior care, a glowup — with a **professional interpreter at every
appointment** and **every price on the table** before you commit. **No foreigner
premium: you pay what a Thai patient pays.** We're the fixers who live here.



## Why people trust us

- **We route only to accredited hospitals.** JCI and Thai HA facilities we've
  vetted — verified at intake, not just advertised.
- **Flat fee, prices posted.** We charge a **published fee, not a cut of your
  procedure** — so we send you to the *best* clinic, never the highest-paying one.
- **A human answers.** Message us and a person — usually a founder — replies within
  a day. No bot, no call-center.
- **No foreigner premium — just a language barrier.** Thai clinics post their prices
  everywhere — on posters, in ads — and openly undercut each other to win you. You
  pay what a Thai patient pays; the only way you'd feel ripped off is not being able
  to read the sign. That's what our translators are for.
- **We tell you when the answer is no.** Surrogacy is banned here; Medicare doesn't
  travel; ADHD stimulants are restricted. We say so, in public, before you spend a
  baht. Straight answers are the whole product.

# Addiction Medicine in Chiang Mai — The Places, Named Plainly
URL: https://defiant.to/addiction/

# Addiction medicine in Chiang Mai — the places, named plainly

Northern Thailand is, quietly, somewhere people come to get treatment for
addiction. This page is a map of the places, not a review of them:
**it ranks nothing and recommends nothing — each facility speaks for
itself.** It is substance-agnostic and judgment-free; whatever brought you
here, the vocabulary and the questions below work the same.

*Not medical advice — Defiant is a concierge, not a clinic, and treatment
decisions belong to you and clinicians. Nothing here evaluates any approach
or predicts any outcome.*

## The shape of what exists

Two kinds, broadly:

**Private residential facilities.** Defiant's mapped directory (nightly
OpenStreetMap refresh) currently carries four named addiction-medicine
residentials in the North and beyond. Contact details below are what the map
itself carries — source: OpenStreetMap.

| Facility | Where | Contact (per OpenStreetMap) |
|---|---|---|
| **Dawn Rehab** | Chiang Mai | — |
| **The River Rehab** | Chiang Mai | +66 95 687 1017 · theriverrehab.com |
| **Siam Rehab** | Mae Chan, Chiang Rai | +66 97 943 6477 · siamrehab.com |
| **Rehab Scandinavia** | Chonburi | rehabscandinavia.com |

**The state and hospital route.** Chiang Mai's public psychiatric hospital,
Suan Prung, operates a rehabilitation centre (ศูนย์ฟื้นฟูสมรรถภาพ, on the
map as **Suan Prung Rehabilitation Center**) — the public-system entry
point, in Thai. **McKean Rehabilitation Center** (สถาบันแมคเคนฯ,
mckeanhosp.org), the century-old mission institution south of the city,
carries "rehabilitation" in its very name; what its rehabilitation services
cover today is a question for its own pages, which we have not yet read
(see below).

## The words to know

- **บำบัด** (*bambat*) — treatment, therapy. The umbrella word; ศูนย์บำบัด is
  a treatment centre.
- **เลิกเหล้า** (*loek lao* — literally "quit liquor") — to stop drinking.
  The plain, everyday phrase; you will see it on public-health posters.
- **ยาเสพติด** (*ya sep tit* — literally "drug one is stuck to") — narcotics,
  addictive drugs. ศูนย์บำบัดยาเสพติด is a drug-treatment centre.
- **ศูนย์ฟื้นฟู** (*sun fuen fu*) — rehabilitation centre; ฟื้นฟู is
  "restore/rehabilitate" and also names Suan Prung's unit above.

## What to ask any facility

Questions, not endorsements — the same list works at every facility:

1. **Licensing.** What license does the facility hold, from which Thai
   authority, and will they show it in writing?
2. **Medical supervision.** Who is medically responsible on site — physicians,
   nurses — at what hours, and what is the arrangement with the nearest
   hospital?
3. **Detox handling.** If medically supervised withdrawal is part of your
   situation, where does it physically happen and under whose care?
4. **Aftercare.** What happens after discharge — follow-up structure,
   coordination with a provider at home?
5. **The full price, itemised, in writing** — ask this of every
   facility on this site.

## What we have not read yet

Every named facility above is on this page because it is on the map — not
because we have completed a sourced read of its own website. Pending
first-hand reads, the same treatment [[=Diabetes|the diabetes page]] got:
Dawn Rehab, The River Rehab, Siam Rehab, Rehab Scandinavia, Suan Prung's
rehabilitation centre, and McKean Rehabilitation Center. Until each read is
done, this page states only what the map states and lets each facility
describe itself.

## FAQ

### Which facility is the best one?

This page does not rank facilities and will not — it ranks nothing and
recommends nothing. The useful work is matching your specific situation
(medical needs, language, budget, duration) against what each facility states
about itself, and asking the questions above. That matching is a
conversation, not a league table.

### Does treatment in Thailand work in English?

The private residentials listed above market internationally; the state route
via Suan Prung runs in Thai. Language is one of the first questions to ask
any facility directly — and interpreters are [[=Translators|a thing Defiant
does]].

### Can Defiant arrange the logistics around treatment?

The travel, visa, interpreter, and paperwork layer — yes; that is what a
concierge is. The clinical choice stays between you and the facility.
[[=Contact|Message us]] or see [[=Concierge|what the concierge costs]].

### What if I just need the medical system, not a residential program?

Then start at [[=Hospitals|the hospital guide]] — psychiatric and internal
medicine departments are ordinary places to start, and เลิกเหล้า / ยาเสพติด
are words every information desk understands.

# Burning Season in Chiang Mai: Dates, Numbers, and the Clean-Air Playbook
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/burning-season/

Every year, roughly from **late January to mid-April**, agricultural burning across the upper Mekong region meets a bowl-shaped valley and a temperature inversion, and Chiang Mai's famously soft air turns hazy. March is usually the peak. By Songkran (mid-April) the rains start rinsing it out, and from May to January the air here is soft mountain air again.

That's the whole calendar. Everything else is numbers and playbook — both below, both live.

## Today's number


> **Chiang Mai air right now:** PM2.5 **3.9 µg/m³** — Very good (US AQI 50). Observed 2026-09-07 15:00. Modelled by CAMS via Open-Meteo — a city-scale model, not a street sensor; treat it as the weather report, not a diagnosis.



| Date | PM2.5 (µg/m³) | Band |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-02 | 15.5 | Good |
| 2026-09-03 | 12.8 | Very good |
| 2026-09-04 | 14.4 | Very good |
| 2026-09-05 | 12.1 | Very good |
| 2026-09-06 | 14.9 | Very good |
| 2026-09-07 | 7.2 | Very good |
| 2026-09-08 | 7.5 | Very good |

*The last seven observed days, same model, generated 2026-09-07.*


Two scales float around town: US AQI (the colored 0–500 number) and micrograms of PM2.5 per cubic meter, which is what Thailand's Pollution Control Department bands run on. This page reports **µg/m³ first** because that's what the Thai advisories, school closure decisions, and your purifier's display all speak.

## The playbook, in the order locals actually do it

1. **Watch the number, not the sky.** Haze photographs worse than it measures some days and better on others. The strip above updates itself; motdang.net keeps [the live city dashboard](https://motdang.net) with the same feed.
2. **Masks: N95 or nothing.** A fitted N95 (หน้ากาก N95, *nâa-gàak* — mask) filters PM2.5; a surgical mask mostly filters your conscience. Pharmacies stock them everywhere — [here's the pharmacy map](/articles/pharmacies-chiang-mai/).
3. **One sealed room with a HEPA purifier.** You don't need to filter the whole house — you need one bedroom where the number is boring. Local supermarkets and Lazada carry HEPA units from about **฿2,500** (*indicative, August 2026*); filters are the recurring cost.
4. **Time your outdoor life.** Early evenings after wind shifts are often the day's best window; mid-morning inversions are often the worst. Check, then run.
5. **Know your exit.** The south — the gulf islands, Phuket, anywhere with sea wind — runs clean while the North burns. Long-stayers routinely book February–April elsewhere and come home for the rains with the [[=DTV|DTV's]] multi-entry runway.

## If you're here for medical care

Timing matters more than most itineraries admit:

- **Respiratory anything** — asthma, COPD, post-COVID lungs — schedule consultations and recovery windows **May through January** if you can. Your lungs and your follow-up appointments will both go smoother.
- **Elective surgery with a long recovery** — the recovery apartment's air quality is part of the surgical plan. Every [[=Concierge|concierge]] recovery briefing between January and April includes a purifier line item; that's not upsell, it's the checklist.
- **Already here and struggling?** The private hospitals on [the hospital map](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/) all run walk-in clinics; smoke-season respiratory visits are the most routine thing they see all year.

*Not medical advice — a logistics note. Breathing decisions belong to you and a physician.*


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## FAQ

### When does burning season start and end in Chiang Mai?
Late January to mid-April, peaking in March, easing with the first real rains around Songkran. Outside that window the air is genuinely good — better than most Western cities' winters.

### Is it safe to visit during burning season?
Millions of people live through it every year with masks, purifiers, and indoor plans. Whether *you* should — with your lungs, your kids, your marathon training — is a live question the daily number answers better than any blog post, this one included.

### Do locals really leave?
Some do — March especially. The DTV and long-stay visas make the seasonal shuffle easy, and the [[=Destinations|destinations pages]] cover the clean-air escapes.

# Chiang Mai Hospitals for Foreigners: The Working Guide
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/

Chiang Mai has one of the best hospital benches in Southeast Asia for a city its size — a university medical school, half a dozen serious private hospitals, and specialty houses for eyes, nerves, and minds. What it doesn't have is a decent map written for the person who just moved here, or who woke up at 2 a.m. deciding whether tonight is an ER night.

This is that map. Numbers are cross-checked against our own city data and dated; when something changes, [tell us](/contact/) and the fix ships the same week.

## The two-sentence version

If it's frightening — chest, breath, head, blood — call **1669** (free, nationwide ambulance) or go straight to the nearest private ER and let them sort the rest out. For everything slower than that, the table below tells you who's good at what, and the [[=Concierge|concierge desk]] can put a real quote in writing before you commit to anything big.

## The hospitals, sorted by a resident


| Hospital | Phone | From Tha Phae Gate | Known for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai** (โรงพยาบาลกรุงเทพ) | 052 089 888 | ~3.5 km | Flagship private — international desk, English-first paperwork |
| **Chiang Mai Ram Hospital** | 053 920 300 | ~1.9 km | The in-town private default; most expats' first ER story ends fine here |
| **Sriphat Medical Center** | 053 946 542 | ~2.1 km | Chiang Mai University's private wing — faculty physicians, university pricing |
| **Maharaj Nakorn (Suan Dok)** (โรงพยาบาลมหาราชนครเชียงใหม่) | 053 936 150 | ~2.1 km | The university mothership — deepest specialist bench in the North, Thai queues, Thai prices |
| **McCormick Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลแมคคอมิก) | 053 921 777 | ~2.1 km | Beloved 130-year mission hospital — calm, capable, gentler bills |
| **Lanna Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลลานนา) | 052 134 777 | ~2.8 km | Private, north side by the Superhighway |
| **Rajavej Chiang Mai Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลราชเวช) | 052 011 999 | ~2.6 km | Walk-in friendly; front desk practised at VA/FMP and insurer paperwork |
| **Central Chiang Mai Memorial Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลเซ็นทรัลเชียงใหม่เมโมเรียล) | 053 819 333 | ~1.7 km | Private, compact, near the old city's south moat |
| **Nakornping Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลนครพิงค์) | 053 999 235 | ~7.7 km | The provincial public hospital, Mae Rim road |
| **Theppanya Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลเทพปัญญา) | 053 852 990 | ~3.2 km | Private, San Sai side of the Superhighway |
| **St. Peter Eye Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลตาเซนต์ปีเตอร์) | 053 225 011 | ~2.7 km | Eyes only — cataract and retina work at Chiang Mai prices |
| **Chiang Mai Neurological Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลประสาทเชียงใหม่) | — | ~2.5 km | Public specialty center for brain and nerve care |

*12 hospitals, curated by residents, coordinates and phones cross-checked against the [Mot Dang](https://motdang.net) map, 2026-09-08. Spot a wrong number? [Report it](/contact/) — fixes land the same week.*


A note on reading it: *private* here (Bangkok, Ram, Lanna, Rajavej, Theppanya, Central Memorial, McCormick) means English at the desk, short queues, card machines, and bills that are real but published. *Public* (Maharaj "Suan Dok", Nakornping) means the deepest specialists in the North at Thai prices, with Thai-first queues that reward patience and a translator — [[=Translators|we know several]].

## What a visit costs

*Indicative, August 2026, confirmed in writing at intake — the standing policy on every number we publish.* A private outpatient visit — doctor, meds, the air-conditioned hour — usually lands between **฿800 and ฿2,500**. A private ER visit with imaging commonly runs **฿3,000–15,000**. Public hospital outpatient care is a few hundred baht and a longer morning. Admission deposits at private hospitals typically start around **฿20,000–50,000**; travel insurance with direct billing makes that line item disappear at the bigger houses.


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## Which hospital for which problem

- **Anything emergent** — nearest 24 h ER, full stop. The [emergency numbers card](/articles/thailand-emergency-numbers/) belongs in your phone today.
- **Complex, rare, or oncology** — Maharaj Nakorn (Suan Dok) carries the university's specialist bench; Sriphat is the same faculty in a private-wing setting with appointments.
- **Orthopedics, cardiac, checkup packages** — Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai and Chiang Mai Ram both run high-volume programs; this is where [[=Procedures|the procedure price pages]] point most often.
- **Eyes** — St. Peter Eye Hospital does cataract and retina work all day, every day.
- **A calm, budget-sane admission** — McCormick has been doing exactly that since 1893.
- **US veterans** — Rajavej's front desk has genuine reps at VA Foreign Medical Program paperwork; [[=VA-FMP|the FMP page]] explains the reimbursement path.

## The air matters here

Respiratory visits track the smoke calendar. If you're planning care with a breathing component — or timing a surgery with a recovery window — read the [burning season guide](/articles/burning-season/) alongside this one.


> **Chiang Mai air right now:** PM2.5 **3.9 µg/m³** — Very good (US AQI 50). Observed 2026-09-07 15:00. Modelled by CAMS via Open-Meteo — a city-scale model, not a street sensor; treat it as the weather report, not a diagnosis.


## FAQ

### Do Chiang Mai hospitals speak English?
At the private hospitals, yes — desks, most physicians, and the billing office. At public hospitals expect Thai first; bring a Thai speaker or [[=Translators|hire one of ours]] for anything with consent forms in it.

### Can I just walk in without a referral?
Yes. Thailand runs on walk-ins; even specialist clinics at private hospitals take same-day patients most mornings. Referrals matter mainly inside the public system.

### Will my travel insurance work?
The big privates (Bangkok, Ram) direct-bill the major insurers; smaller houses may want payment and give you the paperwork to claim back. Either way the itemized bill you leave with is real — that's [[=Recourse|part of how you're protected]] here.

### Which hospital is cheapest?
Public beats private by a wide margin, McCormick is the gentlest of the privates, and every elective quote should be confirmed in writing before you book — which is [[=Concierge|literally the service]].

# LGBTQIA+ Community Flags and Their Meanings
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/community-flags/

![[Pasted image 20250907141552.png]]
### 1. **Progress Pride Flag**

- Combines the rainbow flag with chevrons for trans (blue, pink, white), Black and Brown stripes for people of color.

- Designed by Daniel Quasar (2018).

- Meaning: Inclusion of trans and nonwhite queer people, highlighting intersectionality.


---

### 2. **Rainbow Pride Flag**

- Original LGBTQ+ pride flag, created by Gilbert Baker (1978).

- Current six-stripe version: red (life), orange (healing), yellow (sunlight), green (nature), blue (serenity), violet (spirit).

- Widely recognized symbol of LGBTQ+ pride.


---

### 3. **Nonbinary Pride Flag**

- Yellow, white, purple, black.

- Created by Kye Rowan (2014).

- Meaning:

 - Yellow: outside the gender binary

 - White: many or all genders

 - Purple: mix of male and female

 - Black: no gender


---

### 4. **Genderfluid Pride Flag**

- Pink, white, purple, black, blue stripes.

- Created by JJ Poole (2012).

- Meaning:

 - Pink: femininity

 - White: all genders

 - Purple: mix of masculinity/femininity

 - Black: lack of gender

 - Blue: masculinity


---

### 5. **Transgender Pride Flag**

- Blue, pink, white stripes.

- Created by Monica Helms (1999).

- Meaning:

 - Blue: traditional male

 - Pink: traditional female

 - White: nonbinary, transitioning, or undefined


---

### 6. **Lesbian Pride Flag (Orange-Pink 7-Stripe Version)**

- Orange to pink gradient.

- Updated design (2018) is most common.

- Meaning:

 - Dark orange: gender nonconformity

 - Orange: independence

 - Light orange: community

 - White: unique relationships to womanhood

 - Pink: serenity/peace

 - Dusty rose: love/sex

 - Dark rose: femininity


---

### 7. **Agender Pride Flag**

- Black, gray, white, green.

- Created by Salem X (2014).

- Meaning:

 - Black/white: absence of gender

 - Gray: semi-gender or partial gender

 - Green: nonbinary


---

### 8. **Bisexual Pride Flag**

- Pink, purple, blue.

- Created by Michael Page (1998).

- Meaning:

 - Pink: attraction to same gender

 - Blue: attraction to other genders

 - Purple: overlap/both


---

### 9. **Pansexual Pride Flag**

- Pink, yellow, blue.

- Circulating since ~2010.

- Meaning:

 - Pink: attraction to women

 - Yellow: attraction regardless of gender (nonbinary)

 - Blue: attraction to men


---

### 10. **Polysexual Pride Flag**

- Pink, green, blue.

- Created by Tumblr user “Samlin” (2012).

- Meaning:

 - Pink: attraction to women

 - Green: attraction to nonbinary

 - Blue: attraction to men

# Dental Implants in Thailand: Real Prices, Real Timelines
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/dental-implants-thailand-cost/

Dental implants are the procedure that built Thai medical tourism, and the arithmetic hasn't changed: the same titanium, the same brand catalogs, a dental surgeon who places hundreds a year, and a bill that reads like a typo if you've priced the work in the United States. What has changed is how much nonsense now ranks above the actual numbers. So: the actual numbers, the actual timeline, and the questions that keep a quote real.

## The prices


| Procedure | United States | Thailand | Trip shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Dental Implants](/procedures/dental-implants/) | $3,000–$5,000 per tooth | **$1,000–$1,800 per tooth** | Two trips (placement + crown) or One-trip immediate-load cases |
| [Veneers](/procedures/veneers/) | $1,000–$2,500 per tooth | **$250–$550 per tooth** | 5–8 nights, two visits |
| [Crowns and Bridges](/procedures/crowns-and-bridges/) | $1,000–$2,500 per unit | **$300–$700 per unit** | 4–7 nights |
| [Root Canal Treatment](/procedures/root-canal-treatment/) | $1,000–$2,000 | **$250–$600** | 3–5 nights |
| [Orthodontics (Braces, Aligners)](/procedures/orthodontics-braces-aligners/) | $4,000–$8,000 | **$1,500–$3,500** | Multi-visit over months — expat/long-stay play, not a fly-in |

*Defiant's standing indicative ranges — 2026 published-aggregator figures, every quote confirmed in writing at intake. Full detail on [[=Procedures|the procedure pages]]. Verified 2026-09-08.*



*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## The timeline nobody puts in the headline

A standard implant is **two trips, not one**:

1. **Trip one — placement.** Assessment, 3D imaging, extraction if needed, and the titanium post goes in. A few days in the chair spread over a week or so.
2. **The quiet months.** Osseointegration — the bone knitting to the post — takes **three to six months**. You do this part at home, or on a beach; the implant doesn't care.
3. **Trip two — the crown.** Abutment and crown fitted, bite tuned. Usually under a week.

Single-visit "immediate load" cases exist — good bone, favorable position, and a dentist willing to say so in writing. Treat one-trip promises for ordinary cases the way you'd treat any headline that skips the middle of the story.

Full-arch work (All-on-4, All-on-6) compresses differently: a provisional bridge often goes in fast, with the definitive bridge on a return visit. That's exactly the return-trip rhythm the [follow-up guide](/articles/dtv-medical-runs/) is about — and why the [[=DTV|DTV's]] five years of multi-entry runway pairs so well with dental work.

## What keeps a quote real

Get all four in writing before the flight — this is the whole method, and clinics that do good work answer these happily:

- **The implant line by name.** Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Osstem — brand and model belong on the quote, because they're what any dentist at home will service later.
- **Who places it.** The dental surgeon's name and how many implants they place a year.
- **What the number includes.** Imaging, surgical guide, abutment, crown material, bite adjustments — the unbundled extras are where soft quotes hide.
- **The warranty, portably.** What's covered, for how long, and what documentation travels home with you.

The [[=Concierge|concierge desk]] does this collection as a matter of routine, and [[=Recourse|how you're protected]] explains what the paper trail is for.

## Where the work happens

Bangkok has the giant dedicated centers; Chiang Mai does the same catalog at Chiang Mai overheads — hospital dental departments at [the private hospitals](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/) and standalone implant clinics around the city. The right room depends on your case complexity, your calendar, and where you'd rather spend the quiet months in between.

## FAQ

### How much do dental implants cost in Thailand?
Indicative 2026 range: **$1,000–1,800 per tooth** complete (post, abutment, crown) versus $3,000–5,000 in the US. Full-arch cases quote per jaw and still commonly land under a single US implant-and-crown sequence.

### How long do I need to stay in Thailand for an implant?
About a week for placement, then three to six months of healing wherever you like, then under a week for the crown. Two trips is the standard shape.

### Are Thai dental implants the same brands as in the US?
The major clinics quote the same global catalogs — Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Osstem. That's why the brand belongs on your written quote: any dentist at home can service a known system.

### Is it safe to get dental implants in Thailand?
Implantology is mature, high-volume work here. The safety question is really a selection question — named surgeon, named system, written plan — and that's a solvable one.

---

**Want the numbers for your actual mouth?** The [[=Concierge|concierge desk]] gets named-clinic implant quotes in writing — system, surgeon, inclusions — before you book anything. Questions cost nothing: (reveal button on site)

# Return Trips, Done Right: Follow-Up Care and the DTV Rhythm
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/dtv-medical-runs/

The dirty secret of medical tourism marketing is the singular: *the* trip, *the* procedure, *the* price. Real medicine runs on plurals. Implants want a second visit for the crown. Orthodontics wants a visit every few months. Joint replacements want a six-week review and an annual look. Hormone therapy wants labs on a rhythm. Oncology wants surveillance on a schedule nobody negotiates with. The patients who do this well aren't planning a trip — they're planning a **calendar**.

This page is about the calendar: which procedures come with return trips, how care continues between them, and why Thailand quietly became the easiest place on earth to keep coming back to.

## What the calendar looks like, by procedure

*Typical shapes, not prescriptions — your surgeon's written plan wins, always.*

| Treatment | Trip one | The rhythm after |
|---|---|---|
| [Dental implants](/articles/dental-implants-thailand-cost/) | Placement, ~1 week | Crown trip at 3–6 months; then ordinary dental checkups |
| Orthodontics | Fitting, 1–2 weeks | Adjustment visits every 2–3 months, or a local-dentist hand-off plan |
| Veneers / crowns | One trip, two visits | A years-later polish at most |
| [Joint replacement](/procedures/hip-replacement/) | Surgery + early rehab, 10–14 nights | 6-week review (often local or remote), annual imaging |
| LASIK / cataract | Days | Next-day and one-week checks in-country; then annual eye exams anywhere |
| Hormone therapy | Baseline consult + labs | Blood work every 3–6 months — drawable anywhere, reviewed remotely |
| Checkups / surveillance | [One organized day](/articles/health-checkup-chiang-mai/) | The calendar *is* the treatment — annually, or as advised |

## Continuity is a paperwork problem — solve it on trip one

Follow-up care across borders fails at the filing cabinet, not the operating theater. Before flying home, collect:

- **The itemized bill and operative note in English** — Thai hospitals produce both on request; [[=Recourse|the protection page]] explains why the paper matters.
- **Imaging on disc or download link**, not just the radiologist's summary.
- **The named follow-up plan in writing** — what gets checked, when, and what result would change the plan.
- **A contact that answers** — the international desk's email or LINE, tested once before you leave the building.

With that folder, your doctor at home can run the between-trips reviews, labs can be drawn anywhere, and telemedicine follow-ups with your Thai surgeon become routine instead of improvised. This folder is standard product on every [[=Concierge|concierge]] booking — it's most of what "concierge" means.

## The visa that matches the rhythm

Here's where Thailand lapped the field: the [[=DTV|Destination Thailand Visa]] has a **medical-treatment category** — five years, multiple entry, up to 180 days per stay. That is precisely the shape of a treatment calendar: fly in for placement, home for the quiet months, back for the crown; annual surveillance trips for years on one visa. The mechanics, the paperwork bottleneck, and how to get the treatment-plan letter done right live on [[=DTV|the DTV page]] — the short version is that the visa is easy and the clinic paperwork is the craft.

Timing the return trips is its own small art: the [festival calendar](/articles/songkran-medical-timing/) and [burning season](/articles/burning-season/) pages are the two screens worth a glance before you pick the week.


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## FAQ

### How does follow-up care work after medical treatment abroad?
On paper you carry home: operative notes, imaging, and a written follow-up plan in English. Routine reviews then split between your home doctor, remote consults with the treating surgeon, and scheduled return trips for the milestones that need hands.

### Do I have to fly back to Thailand for follow-ups?
Only for the milestones that need the chair — an implant crown, an adjustment, an annual look. Labs and reviews in between run locally or remotely when the plan is written down properly on trip one.

### What visa covers repeated medical trips to Thailand?
The DTV's medical category: five years, multiple entry, 180 days per stay. One visa carries an entire treatment calendar of return visits.

### What should I get in writing before leaving the hospital?
The itemized bill, the operative note, your imaging, the follow-up schedule, and a tested contact channel — the five-line folder that makes every later conversation easy.

# Health Checkup Packages in Chiang Mai: What ฿ Buys You
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/health-checkup-chiang-mai/

Thailand treats the annual checkup as a retail product, and it's one of the country's best ideas. Private hospitals publish package menus the way restaurants publish set lunches: named tiers, listed inclusions, posted prices, same-week appointments. No referral, no prior authorization, no mystery bill four months later. For the price of a US copay-and-deductible adventure, you leave with a bound English report and every number that matters.

## The tiers, decoded

*Indicative Chiang Mai private-hospital ranges, August 2026 — menus vary by hospital and get confirmed when you book.*

| Tier | Typically includes | Indicative price |
|---|---|---|
| **Basic** | Physical exam, CBC, glucose, lipids, kidney and liver panels, urinalysis, chest X-ray, ECG | **฿2,500–5,000** |
| **Standard** | Everything above + ultrasound (abdomen), thyroid, uric acid, stool exam, hepatitis screen | **฿5,000–10,000** |
| **Executive** | Everything above + tumor markers, cardiac stress test or echo, bone density, eye and hearing screens | **฿10,000–25,000** |
| **Add-ons** | Colonoscopy, CT calcium scoring, sleep study, sexual-health panels — priced à la carte | ask the menu |

Package medicine has one caveat worth saying plainly: screening menus love tests that photograph well. A checkup is a snapshot, not a diagnosis, and a good physician conversation about the results — included at every hospital here — is the part that turns numbers into decisions. *Not medical advice; bring your own doctor into the loop for what to screen and how often.*


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## Where to book it


| Hospital | Phone | From Tha Phae Gate | Known for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai** (โรงพยาบาลกรุงเทพ) | 052 089 888 | ~3.5 km | Flagship private — international desk, English-first paperwork |

| **McCormick Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลแมคคอมิก) | 053 921 777 | ~2.1 km | Beloved 130-year mission hospital — calm, capable, gentler bills |
| **Lanna Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลลานนา) | 052 134 777 | ~2.8 km | Private, north side by the Superhighway |
| **Rajavej Chiang Mai Hospital** (โรงพยาบาลราชเวช) | 052 011 999 | ~2.6 km | Walk-in friendly; front desk practised at VA/FMP and insurer paperwork |

*12 hospitals, curated by residents, coordinates and phones cross-checked against the [Mot Dang](https://motdang.net) map, 2026-09-08. Spot a wrong number? [Report it](/contact/) — fixes land the same week.*


Every private hospital on the table runs a checkup center; Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai and Chiang Mai Ram have the biggest package menus, Sriphat brings university faculty to the readout, and McCormick prices gentlest. The [hospital guide](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/) covers who's good at what beyond the checkup counter.

## How the day actually goes

1. **Book a day or two ahead** — phone, LINE, or walk in and pick a morning. Fast overnight (usually 8–12 hours; water is fine) for the blood panel.
2. **Arrive early, wear two-piece clothing,** bring your passport and any home lab results for comparison.
3. **The circuit takes two to four hours** — stations, not waiting rooms. Most results land the same day; imaging reads may take another day.
4. **Ask for the English report** when you book, not after. Every hospital above produces one; saying it early makes it seamless.
5. **The physician readout is included.** Bring questions. This is also the cheapest specialist referral system on earth — anything flagged gets a same-building follow-up at Chiang Mai prices.

## Making a trip of it

A checkup pairs naturally with everything else on this site: schedule it at the front of a [[=Procedures|procedure trip]] as the pre-op baseline, or fly it solo as the annual ritual — the [[=DTV|DTV]] crowd books next year's on the way out. If you're timing a visit, the [festival calendar](/articles/songkran-medical-timing/) and [burning season guide](/articles/burning-season/) are the two calendars worth checking first.

## FAQ

### How much is a full health checkup in Chiang Mai?
Indicative August 2026: basic packages ฿2,500–5,000, standard ฿5,000–10,000, executive ฿10,000–25,000. The menu is posted; the price is the price.

### Do I need an appointment for a health checkup in Thailand?
A day or two ahead is plenty at most hospitals; some take same-day walk-ins if you've fasted. Booking gets you the English report and a smoother morning.

### Will the results be in English?
Yes — ask when you book. The bound English report is standard product at Chiang Mai's private hospitals and travels well to doctors at home.

### How long does a hospital checkup take?
Two to four hours for the circuit, with most results the same day and the physician readout included before you leave.

# Massage in Chiang Mai: 294 Shops, Sorted by a Local
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/massage-chiang-mai/

Chiang Mai is the massage capital of a massage country. The old city alone holds more registered shops than most Western cities hold in total, the northern school of Thai massage has its own lineage, and an hour of skilled work costs less than a cinema ticket back home. The problem was never finding a massage — it's knowing which of the five kinds you're about to get, what the fair posted rate is, and how to ask for softer without a phrasebook.

All three, below.

## The map says


**1317 massage shops** sit on the household map of Chiang Mai — 1060 with a working phone number. A sampler across town:

| Shop | Phone | Find it |
|---|---|---|
| **11O1 health club & co พิลาทิส สตูดิโอ เชียงใหม่** | 086 605 6906 | 110 ถนน ป่าตัน |
| **1678 Massage** | 063 579 9588 | 24/4 NimmanSoi13, Nimmanahaeminda Road |
| **168 Nails & Salon กาดฝรั่งแม่ริม** | 098 351 6888 | กาดฝรั่งแม่ริม ต.แม่สา อ.แม่ริม จ.เชียงใหม่ |
| **20 บาท กาดสวนแก้ว - ชั้น 2 ฝั่ง playland และ นวดไทย** | 081 724 6369 | ~2.1 km from Tha Phae Gate |
| **2B Relax massage Chiang Mai ( Thunghotel )** | 065 473 5687 | 302 Tunghotel Rd |
| **2eyes Studio ต่อขนตา สักคิ้วแม่สาย** | 084 655 2441 | 315 หมู่7 ต.แม่สาย อ.แม่สาย จ.เชียงราย |
| **2eyes studio สักคิ้ว ต่อขนตาแม่สาย** | 084 655 2441 | ~206.5 km from Tha Phae Gate |

*Counts and rows from [Mot Dang](https://motdang.net)'s curated set, 2026-09-08. The full map is free: [motdang.net](https://motdang.net).*


## The menu, decoded

First-use Thai, with rough romanization — say it slowly and any shop will smile and take it from there:

| On the sign | Say it | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| นวดแผนไทย | *nûat phǎen thai* | Traditional Thai massage: clothed (loose pajamas provided), no oil — pressing, rocking, and assisted stretches along the body's energy lines |
| นวดเท้า | *nûat tháo* | Foot massage: an armchair, an hour, cream, and the walking day you deserved |
| นวดน้ำมัน | *nûat nám-man* | Oil massage: table, towels, long strokes — closer to Swedish |
| นวดประคบ | *nûat prà-khóp* | Hot herbal compress: steamed bundles (ลูกประคบ, *lûuk prà-khóp*) of ginger, turmeric, and lemongrass pressed along the muscles |
| นวดจับเส้น | *nûat jàp sên* | "Holding the lines" — old-school deep work along tendons and nerve lines; the strong stuff, ask for it by name |

The North also keeps ย่ำขาง (*yâm khǎang*) — a Lanna healing practice where the therapist works with a heated plough blade and oiled foot. You'll find it at traditional healing houses rather than storefront shops; it's a cultural experience as much as a treatment, and worth seeking out sober-minded and curious.

## What it costs

*Posted rates around town, August 2026 — indicative, and the sign wins.* A storefront Thai massage runs **฿200–400 per hour**; add ฿50–150 for the foot-massage chair hour. Oil work posts **฿300–600** at shops, **฿600–1,200** at proper spas. Hotel and destination spas price **฿800–2,500+** for the same hour with better robes and a gong. Herbal compress adds **฿100–300** anywhere. Tipping **฿50–100** on a shop massage is normal and landed; spas fold service charges in.

Asking whether a price is แพง (*phaeng* — expensive) is normal Thai small talk, not rudeness. The posted rate is the posted rate; nobody haggles a massage board.


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## The etiquette nobody writes down

- **Softer / harder:** เบา ๆ (*bao bao*) is softer; หนัก ๆ (*nàk nàk*) is harder. Both work mid-stroke, no offense taken, ever.
- **Shower first for oil work** — it's courtesy, and good shops offer one.
- **Say what hurts before you start.** Point. Therapists here adjust around injuries all day; the word for pain is เจ็บ (*jèp*).
- **The cracking is optional.** Thai massage traditionally ends with back and neck work that can include joint cracks — wave a hand and say no and it simply doesn't happen.
- **Eat light, arrive early, silence the phone.** The hour works better when you're not digesting a khao soi against it.

## When massage is actually rehab

If you're here around a surgery — [[=Procedures|orthopedic work especially]] — there's a real difference between a relaxation massage and clinical soft-tissue work. Post-operative anything belongs with the physical therapists first: [[=Physiotherapy|the physio page]] covers session-rate rehab, and the [[=Concierge|concierge desk]] sequences surgeon → physio → massage in the right order with the surgeon's sign-off.

## FAQ

### How much is a one-hour Thai massage in Chiang Mai?
฿200–400 at storefront shops as of August 2026, more at spas. The posted board is the price.

### Do I need to book ahead?
Storefronts, almost never — walk in. Destination spas and famous shops, yes, a day or two, especially December–February.

### Is Thai massage safe after surgery or with a medical condition?
That's a physician conversation, not a footnote — bring it to your surgeon or doctor first, and start with clinical physio rather than a shop when in doubt.

### What's the difference between Thai massage and oil massage?
Thai massage is clothed pressure-and-stretch on a floor mat; oil massage is a table, towels, and long strokes. Different traditions, different afternoons.

# Pharmacies in Chiang Mai: What You Can Buy, and Where, at 2 a.m.
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/pharmacies-chiang-mai/

The green cross is one of Thailand's great everyday mercies. A ร้านขายยา (*ráan khǎai yaa* — pharmacy) sits on nearly every commercial block, a licensed pharmacist stands behind the counter through the posted hours, and a striking amount of routine medicine is dispensed on the spot, at posted prices, in two minutes, without an appointment.

Here's how the system works, and where the counters are.

## How Thai pharmacies work

Thai law sorts medicines into tiers, and the tier — not the shop — decides what you walk out with:

- **General-sale medicines** — paracetamol, antihistamines, rehydration salts, motion-sickness tablets, most topicals — are open-shelf. Convenience stores carry a legal mini-set of these for the 2 a.m. run.
- **Pharmacist-dispensed medicines** — a wide middle tier that includes many things Americans expect a prescription for — are handed over after a short consult with the on-duty pharmacist. Describe the problem; they'll ask sensible questions.
- **Prescription-only and controlled medicines** — psychiatric meds, sleep meds in the controlled classes, strong painkillers, and similar — require a doctor and usually a hospital pharmacy. A storefront that offers these without paperwork is telling you something about itself; walk on.

Two practical notes. Bring the **generic name** (the international one, not the US brand) for anything you take — the box here will carry the generic or a Thai brand. And pharmacist hours are roughly **9:00–21:00**; outside them, the 24 h counters live inside the private hospitals on [the hospital guide](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/).

## What it costs

*Indicative posted prices, August 2026.* A blister of paracetamol is **฿10–20**. Common generics — antihistamines, simple antibiotics when dispensed, stomach medicines — mostly land **฿30–200** per course. Imported brands cost import-brand money. Nothing about the counter is a negotiation; prices are marked or quoted flat, and asking the price first is ordinary Thai manners.


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*

**616 pharmacies** are on Defiant's Thailand-wide directory; **161** of them are in the Chiang Mai basin. The ten closest to Tha Phae Gate (ประตูท่าแพ, *pratu Tha Phae* — the old city's front door):

| Pharmacy | From Tha Phae Gate |
|---|---|

| คลังยาท่าแพ | ~0.1 km |
| พีระ | ~0.1 km |

| Pharma Square | ~0.1 km |
| ร้านเภสัชกร ฟาม่าช้อย | ~0.2 km |

*From Defiant's nightly OpenStreetMap refresh, distances computed straight-line, 2026-09-08. A missing shop is a [fixable report](/contact/).*


## When the pharmacy is the wrong counter

Pharmacists here are genuinely skilled triage — and they'll say so themselves when something needs a doctor. Fevers that persist, anything cardiac, anything neurological, prescriptions that need continuity: that's clinic territory, same-day and inexpensive here. [The hospital guide](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/) shows where to walk in, and for care you're planning ahead of a trip, the [[=Concierge|concierge desk]] gets quotes in writing first.

*Not medical advice — an operating manual for a counter. Medication decisions belong to you and licensed professionals.*

## FAQ

### Can I buy antibiotics over the counter in Thailand?
Many common ones are pharmacist-dispensed after a consult at the counter — legal here, surprising to Americans. The pharmacist can and will decline when a doctor is the right call.

### Can I refill my home prescription in Thailand?
Bring the generic name and your home paperwork. Routine medicines are often dispensable; controlled classes need a Thai doctor's prescription — a clinic visit here is fast and inexpensive, and continuity beats improvisation.

### Is there a 24-hour pharmacy in Chiang Mai?
The dependable 24 h counters are the private hospital pharmacies. Between the convenience-store shelf tier and those, the city is covered around the clock.

### Are medicines in Thailand real?
At licensed green-cross pharmacies and hospital counters, yes — Thailand's FDA regulates the supply tightly. The caution zone is unlicensed stalls and anything that arrives by direct message.

# Physical Therapy in Chiang Mai: The Clinic Map and the Session Math
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/physiotherapy-chiang-mai/

Rehab is arithmetic. A knee replacement wants a course of sessions, not a session; a shoulder wants months of them. At US clinic rates that arithmetic quietly amputates the back half of most recovery plans — people stop going when the copays outrun the progress. Chiang Mai's quiet superpower is that the arithmetic works: session rates low enough to *finish the course*, with unhurried one-on-one hours the Western clinic model can't afford anymore.

[[=Physiotherapy|The physiotherapy overview]] makes the whole-country case. This page is the Chiang Mai working sheet: the clinic map and the session math.

## The clinics, mapped


**7 physiotherapy and physical-rehab facilities** are on Defiant's mapped directory. The closest to Tha Phae Gate:

| Clinic | From Tha Phae Gate |
|---|---|
| Physical Therapy Centre | ~1.8 km |

*From Defiant's nightly OpenStreetMap refresh, straight-line distances, 2026-09-08. Hospital physio departments ride on [the hospital guide](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/).*


Three settings, three flavors:

- **Hospital physio departments** — machine-rich (ultrasound, shockwave, hydrotherapy at the big houses), surgeon in the same building, records in one file. The natural home for post-surgical courses; every hospital on [the hospital guide](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/) runs one.
- **Standalone clinics** — the mapped rows above; licensed physios (นักกายภาพบำบัด, *nák gaai-yá-phâap bam-bàt* — physical therapist), longer hours, easier walk-in rhythm, often stronger English in the tourist-adjacent blocks.
- **Home visits** — a physio comes to the recovery apartment with a folding table. For the first weeks after joint work, this is the difference between doing the exercises and describing them.

## The session math

*Indicative Chiang Mai rates, August 2026 — posted or quoted flat, confirmed when you book.*

| Setting | Indicative per session |
|---|---|
| Standalone clinic (45–60 min, one-on-one) | **฿600–1,200** |
| Hospital physio department (with modalities) | **฿700–1,500** |
| Home visit | **฿800–1,500** |
| Course packages (10 sessions, commonly discounted) | ask — 10–20% off is normal |

Now the part that matters: a **20-session course** — a real post-op arc, not a gesture — lands around **฿15,000–25,000** all-in. Price the same course at home, remember you'd also be driving to it, and the recovery-in-Thailand model explains itself.


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## How the sequence works after surgery

1. **The surgeon writes the plan** — frequency, restrictions, milestones. If the operation happened here, the physio department is downstairs and the referral is same-day.
2. **Front-load the supervised weeks.** Daily or near-daily early sessions beat weekly heroics; this is where Chiang Mai rates change what's possible.
3. **Graduate to a program** — clinics here are generous with written home programs and video check-ins once you've earned independence.
4. **Flying home mid-course?** Leave with the progress notes in English and the exercise program documented — the hand-off is a paperwork problem, and paperwork problems are solvable ones.

For the recovery weeks themselves: [massage is the reward, physio is the plan](/articles/massage-chiang-mai/) — in that order, with the surgeon's blessing on both.

## FAQ

### How much does physiotherapy cost in Chiang Mai?
Indicative August 2026: ฿600–1,500 per one-on-one session depending on setting, with course packages commonly discounted. A full 20-session post-op course runs around ฿15,000–25,000.

### Do I need a referral for physio in Thailand?
Standalone clinics take direct bookings for most musculoskeletal work. Post-surgical courses should run on the surgeon's written plan — which any hospital here produces as a matter of routine.

### Do Chiang Mai physiotherapists speak English?
At hospital departments and the established standalone clinics, working English is the norm, and demonstration carries the rest. Say what hurts; point; they take it from there.

### Can I do surgery and rehab in one Thailand trip?
That's the model at its best — operate, then spend the supervised weeks recovering at rates that let you finish the course. The [[=Concierge|concierge desk]] sequences exactly this.

# Choosing Senior Care in Chiang Mai: The Vetting Visit, Step by Step
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/senior-care-chiang-mai/

The case for Chiang Mai senior care — the staffing ratios, the gardens, the monthly rates that don't devour an estate — is made on [[=Senior-Living|the senior living page]], numbers and caveats included. This page is the next step: you're persuaded enough to look, and now somebody has to actually *choose*. That somebody is usually a family member with one week in Thailand and no checklist.

Here's the checklist. Good homes answer all of it gladly — that's rather the point.

## The facilities, mapped


**11 senior-care and geriatric facilities** sit on Defiant's mapped directory around Chiang Mai:

| Facility | From Tha Phae Gate |
|---|---|
| พีดีเนอร์สซิ่งโฮม ดูแลผู้สูงอายุ | ~4.1 km |
| ศูนย์เวชศาสตร์ผู้สูงอายุ เชียงใหม่ | ~4.3 km |
| Helping Hands Nursing Home | ~4.6 km |
| Kanya Nursing Home | ~5.8 km |
| สถานสงเคราะห์คนชราวัยทองนิเวศน์ | ~38.7 km |

*From Defiant's nightly OpenStreetMap refresh, 2026-09-08. Distance matters twice here — for the family visit, and for the [hospital run](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/).*


## The vetting visit, step by step

**Come twice: once announced, once not.** The scheduled tour shows you the best day; the unannounced drop-in (mid-afternoon is telling) shows you the ordinary one. Facilities comfortable with both are telling you something good about themselves.

**1. Count the hands.**
- Carers per resident, day shift and — ask separately — **night shift**.
- Is a **registered nurse on site or on call** overnight? Which, exactly?
- Who does personal care, and how is dignity handled — same-gender option, closed doors, unhurried pace?

**2. Watch five minutes of ordinary time.** Are residents parked in front of a TV or engaged? Do staff address them by name, in which language, and does anyone kneel to wheelchair height to talk? You can't fake the texture of an ordinary afternoon.

**3. Ask the medication questions.**
- Who dispenses, who double-checks, and where is it charted?
- How do prescriptions renew — which doctor, which hospital, how often reviewed?
- For dementia care: how are behavioral medications decided, and **who consents**?

**4. Walk the hospital run.** The map above gives the distance; drive it. Which [hospital](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/) does the home use for emergencies, who accompanies the resident, and how fast does the family hear? Ask for the last real example — good homes have one and tell it plainly.

**5. Read the money mechanics like a lease.**
- What does the monthly rate include — and what's à la carte (diapers, physio, transport, hospital escorts)?
- Deposit, notice period, and the terms if care needs escalate or the resident passes.
- How are bills presented, in which language and currency? *Rates and bands live on [[=Senior-Living|the senior living page]]; every figure gets confirmed in writing here too.*

**6. Test the family loop.** Photos and video calls on what rhythm? Who answers WhatsApp or LINE messages, and how fast, in English? Ask for a reference family in your time zone — the established homes happily connect you.

**7. Trial month before commitment.** The good operators offer one and recommend it themselves. It answers more than every brochure combined.


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## The language question, answered early

Care is bilingual work here: hands-on staff are Thai, senior staff at expat-serving homes work in English (several are European-run), and the charts can be kept in both — ask to see one. A parent who still charms in English will be answered in kind; a parent slipping into an older tongue will be met with more patience here than most systems anywhere can offer. The [[=Translators|translator bench]] covers the paperwork moments.

## FAQ

### How do I choose a nursing home in Chiang Mai from abroad?
Shortlist from the mapped facilities, video-tour first, then make one in-person vetting trip with the checklist above — announced visit, unannounced visit, hospital run, trial month. The whole loop fits in a week.

### What questions should I ask a Thai senior-care facility?
Night staffing, nurse coverage, medication charting, the emergency-hospital story, all-in versus à-la-carte pricing, and the family-communication rhythm — the seven steps above, in writing where it matters.

### Can families do a trial stay before committing?
The established homes offer a trial month and encourage it. Treat reluctance about trials as an answer in itself.

### Who handles medical care for residents?
The home manages daily care and medication routines; doctors come on rounds or residents travel to their hospital — ask which hospital, how far, and who escorts. The map above shows the distances.

# The Festival Calendar That Should Schedule Your Surgery
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/songkran-medical-timing/

Thai hospitals never close. Emergency rooms run through every holiday on the calendar, and that calendar is one of the richest on earth. But *around* the ER, the country genuinely reshapes itself several times a year — clinic schedules thin, surgeons travel like everyone else, flights fill, and for three days in April the entire nation holds a water fight. If you're flying in for treatment, the festival calendar isn't trivia. It's scheduling data.

## The fixed dates


| Date | Holiday | What it means for a medical trip |
|---|---|---|
| **Jan 1** | New Year's Day | Elective clinics thin; ERs normal |
| **Apr 13–15** | Songkran (Thai New Year) | The big one — elective slates pause, travel peaks, water everywhere |
| **May 1** | Labour Day | Private-sector holiday; hospital OPD mostly normal |
| **May 4** | Coronation Day | Government offices closed; visa desks too |
| **Jun 3** | Queen Suthida's Birthday | Public holiday |
| **Jul 28** | King's Birthday | Public holiday |
| **Aug 12** | Mother's Day (Queen Sirikit's Birthday) | Public holiday |
| **Oct 13** | King Bhumibol Memorial Day | Public holiday |
| **Oct 23** | Chulalongkorn Day | Public holiday |
| **Dec 5** | Father's Day (King Bhumibol's Birthday) | Public holiday |
| **Dec 10** | Constitution Day | Public holiday |
| **Dec 31** | New Year's Eve | Travel peaks; book transport early |

*Fixed-date national holidays. Buddhist observances (Makha Bucha, Visakha Bucha, Asalha Bucha, Loy Krathong / Yi Peng) follow the lunar calendar — announced dates appear below when official. Verified 2026-09-08.*



*No festival dates are officially announced right now (2026-09-06). When organizers publish, the confirmed dates appear here automatically — the fixed national holidays above never move.*


## What actually changes on a holiday

- **ERs: nothing.** 24 hours, every day of the year — the [emergency card](/articles/thailand-emergency-numbers/) works on Songkran morning exactly as it does in November.
- **Outpatient clinics thin out.** Specialist OPD sessions shrink or pause on national holidays, and the private-clinic evening sessions many hospital physicians run go quiet. The days *around* a holiday book heavier as everyone reschedules.
- **Elective surgery slates pause** around the big ones — surgeons take holidays too, and post-op reviews need the team present. Plan the operation a comfortable week clear of Songkran, not the Friday before it.
- **Government offices close on every official date** — visa extensions, document legalization, and anything at an amphoe (อำเภอ, *amphoe* — district office) waits until the next business day.
- **Transport and hotels peak** at Songkran and New Year. Book both early or arrive after the wave.
- **Buddhist observance days** (Makha Bucha, Visakha Bucha, Asalha Bucha) pause alcohol sales nationwide — a footnote for most patients, a planning note for a celebration dinner.

## The Songkran rule for fresh wounds

Songkran (สงกรานต์, *sǒng-graan* — Thai New Year, April 13–15) deserves its own paragraph. It is joyous, national, and **wet**: for several days, everyone outdoors gets soaked, cheerfully and without exemption. Moat water, ice water, water from strangers on pickup trucks. If you'll be carrying fresh incisions, dressings, or a healing implant in mid-April, plan to be somewhere quiet, or somewhere else — surgical wounds and festival water are a combination no surgeon will bless. Schedule the operation for late April instead and come back for the fun next year, healed.

## The good windows

Put the pieces together and the smooth seasons pick themselves:

- **May–June** — post-Songkran, pre-rain-peak, cool bills, quiet clinics, soft green mountains.
- **September–November** — the year's sweet spot: rains easing, air clean, full clinic schedules, and Yi Peng's lanterns as the reward at the end of recovery. Book November lodging early.
- **December–January works** with light planning around New Year's week.
- **February–April** carries two calendars at once — the holiday wave *and* [burning season](/articles/burning-season/). It's all manageable; it's just the season where planning earns its keep.

## FAQ

### When is Songkran in Thailand?
April 13–15, every year — the official national holiday. Celebrations in Chiang Mai often stretch a few days longer around the moat.

### Are hospitals in Thailand open during Songkran?
Emergency rooms, fully — 24 hours, as always. Outpatient clinics and elective surgery schedules thin around the holiday and refill quickly after.

### What is the best time of year for medical treatment in Thailand?
May–June and September–November combine full clinic schedules, clean air, and easy logistics. The engine behind this page keeps the holiday table current, so check it against your dates.

### Do Thai holidays affect visa services?
Yes — immigration and government offices close on every official holiday. Extensions and paperwork belong on the business days around them.

# "Stellate Ganglion Block in Thailand: The Ten-Minute Injection That Turns Down the Alarm"
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/stellate-ganglion-block-thailand/

There is a knot of nerve tissue at the base of your neck, roughly level with the top of your collarbone, called the stellate ganglion. It is a junction box for the sympathetic nervous system — the branch that runs your fight-or-flight response, your heart rate, your flushing, your sweating, and the sensation people describe as *bracing for something*.

A stellate ganglion block is a small volume of local anesthetic placed around that junction box under ultrasound guidance. The needle goes in, the sympathetic traffic to your head, neck, and upper chest quiets down for a few hours, and in a meaningful number of people something stays quieter for far longer than the anesthetic itself lasts.

It is one of the stranger procedures in modern medicine, and one of the more interesting. It is also a fraction of the US price here.

## What the sympathetic nervous system has to do with any of this

The reason a neck injection turns up in conversations about trauma, menopause, and pain is that all three route through the same wiring.

Sympathetic outflow to the head and upper body passes through the cervicothoracic chain. Turn the volume down at that junction and you affect a surprising spread of things at once: vascular tone in the face and scalp, the thermoregulatory flushing behind a hot flash, the baseline arousal that makes a startle response fire early, and the sympathetic maintenance of certain pain states.

The leading hypothesis for why relief outlasts the anesthetic is that the block gives an overactive system a period of quiet long enough to reset its own set point — and, in the trauma literature specifically, that reduced sympathetic input dampens amygdala reactivity. That remains a hypothesis. The clinical effect is measured more confidently than the mechanism is explained, which is a normal state of affairs in medicine and worth saying plainly.

## What it's used for, graded

Defiant grades the science on every procedure page, and this one has genuinely different evidence at different indications. Treating them as one thing is where most of the internet goes wrong.

| Use | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Upper-limb and facial nerve pain, CRPS | **Established** | The original indication. Decades of use, both diagnostic and therapeutic. |
| Refractory ventricular arrhythmia | **Established, narrow** | A cardiology rescue technique in specialist hands. Not an outpatient request. |
| PTSD | **Reasonable** | Several randomized trials, results mixed but net positive. Adopted within US military and veterans' medicine. |
| Menopausal hot flashes | **Promising, small** | Multiple small randomized trials show reduced frequency and severity, studied especially in women who cannot take estrogen. |
| Shingles pain, phantom limb, Raynaud's | **Supportive** | Long clinical tradition, smaller literature. |
| Dysautonomia, POTS, post-viral autonomic syndromes | **Experimental** | Case series and small cohorts, much of it post-COVID. Mechanistically coherent, not yet proven. |

If a clinic markets this as a cure for a long list of conditions, that is a signal about the clinic. The procedure is real; the indication list is where care is required.

## What the appointment is actually like

This is the part nobody describes well, so here it is in order.

You lie on your back with your head turned slightly away from the side being treated. The area is cleaned and numbed. The doctor — an anesthesiologist, almost always — uses ultrasound to see the vessels, the thyroid, and the muscle planes, then places a thin needle to the front of the transverse process of the sixth or seventh cervical vertebra and injects a few millilitres of local anesthetic.

Needle time is under ten minutes. You are awake throughout.

Then the odd part. Within a few minutes your eyelid on that side droops, the pupil narrows, that nostril congests, your eye may water, and the side of your face feels warm and flushed. This is Horner's syndrome, and far from being a complication it is the confirmation that the block landed where it was aimed. Your voice may go hoarse and swallowing may feel strange, because the anesthetic spreads near the nerve that runs your larynx.

All of it wears off over a few hours. You are observed for a while, told not to eat or drink until swallowing feels normal, and told not to drive yourself home.

For trauma indications the common protocol is right-sided, and often two blocks rather than one — the second days to a couple of weeks after the first.

## Risks, stated straight

Ultrasound guidance changed the risk profile of this procedure substantially, because the operator can see the carotid, the vertebral artery, the lung apex, and the thyroid rather than working from surface landmarks alone.

Genuine risks remain and belong in the conversation: injection into a blood vessel, bleeding around the airway, and puncture of the top of the lung. All are uncommon; all are why this belongs to an anesthesiologist with an ultrasound and a proper facility rather than to a wellness clinic with a treatment room. Temporary hoarseness, a heavy-feeling arm, and the Horner's picture are expected effects, not problems.

Ask two questions when you book: is it ultrasound-guided, and how many does this doctor do a year. Both answers should come easily.

## How long it lasts

Wide range, and the range is the truth. Some people get weeks. Some get months. A year of benefit from a single block is on the good end of reported outcomes but well within what happens.

Because the procedure is repeatable and comparatively inexpensive here, a durable responder can simply have it again when the effect fades. That arithmetic looks very different in Thailand than it does under a US deductible, and it is a large part of why this article exists.

## What it costs

In the United States a single block commonly runs several hundred to a couple of thousand dollars, and coverage is inconsistent — pain and cardiac indications are often covered, trauma and vasomotor indications frequently are not, which puts the full amount on the patient.

Thai pricing for interventional pain procedures typically lands at a small fraction of the US figure, in line with how the rest of this site's price comparisons run. Defiant does not publish a baht number it has not collected, and quotes for this specific procedure are being gathered now — this line updates when they land. Ask for the quote in writing, and ask whether it covers the anesthesiologist, the ultrasound, the facility, and the observation period as one number or four.


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## Where to ask in Thailand

This is a pain-medicine procedure, so the department you want is anesthesiology, and the clinic you want is a คลินิกระงับปวด (*khlínìk rá-ngáp pùat* — pain clinic). Ask for it by the English name; the term is standard among Thai anesthesiologists and does not need translating.

**In Chiang Mai**, the strongest odds are with the university teaching hospital's anesthesiology service, which carries the widest interventional range in the north; the large private hospitals are the faster route when they have a pain specialist on staff. Availability moves with individual doctors rather than with buildings, so the question to ask is *which doctor*, not *which hospital*. [The hospital guide](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/) has the phone numbers.

**In Bangkok**, the major teaching hospitals and the international private hospitals all run established interventional pain services, and this is a routine part of their repertoire. If Chiang Mai comes back thin, a Bangkok trip is short and the appointment is a single day.

**Bring your records.** A documented prior response to a stellate ganglion block is the single most useful thing you can hand a new doctor. It converts a long explanation into one line of history and changes the whole tenor of the consultation.

## When it is the wrong tool

A block quiets a signal. It does not do the work that the signal was pointing at.

For trauma, the strongest results in the literature come when a block is paired with therapy rather than substituting for it — the quiet period is what makes the other work possible. For hot flashes, hormone therapy and the non-hormonal options are first-line for most people, and this is the interesting second-line choice, particularly for women who cannot take estrogen. For orthostatic symptoms, get the measurements first: a ten-minute stand test with a blood-pressure cuff costs nothing and tells a doctor more than a paragraph of description.

And anything that is undiagnosed should be diagnosed before it is blocked.

*Not medical advice — a briefing on a procedure. Every decision here belongs to you and a licensed doctor who has examined you.*

## FAQ

### Is a stellate ganglion block painful?
Less than most people expect. The skin is numbed first, and needle time is under ten minutes. The strange part is the hours afterward — a drooping eyelid and a warm, flushed face — rather than the injection itself.

### How long does a stellate ganglion block last?
Anywhere from weeks to a year or more. The anesthetic itself wears off the same day; any benefit past that comes from the system settling at a lower baseline. Repeat blocks are routine when the effect fades.

### Is it available in Thailand?
Yes, as a pain-medicine procedure at hospitals with an interventional anesthesiology service. Bangkok's major centers do it routinely; in Chiang Mai it depends on which pain specialists are currently practising, so ask for a named doctor.

### Does it work for PTSD?
The randomized evidence is mixed but net positive, and it is used within US military and veterans' medicine. It works best alongside therapy rather than instead of it, and it does not help everyone.

### Can it help hot flashes?
Several small randomized trials say yes, with reduced frequency and severity. It is studied most in women who cannot take estrogen. The evidence base is real but smaller than the hormone-therapy literature.

### Why does my eyelid droop afterwards?
Because the block worked. Horner's syndrome — droopy lid, small pupil, stuffy nostril, warm face on that side — is the expected confirmation that the anesthetic reached the ganglion. It resolves within hours.

# Thailand Emergency Numbers: The One-Page Card That Works
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/thailand-emergency-numbers/

Thailand does not use 911, and the number that matters most — **1669**, the national medical emergency line — is one most visitors have never seen written down. This page is the card. Save the share image, screenshot the tables, send it to the person you travel with. It's built to be useful before you ever need it, which is the only good time.

## The card


| Number | Who answers | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **1669** | Medical emergency / ambulance | Free, 24 h, nationwide — the one to save |
| **1155** | Tourist police | English spoken, 24 h |
| **191** | Police | Any emergency, Thai-first |
| **199** | Fire & rescue | 24 h |

*National numbers, verified 2026-09-08. Save 1669 before you need it.*


**1669** dispatches free public ambulances nationwide, 24 hours. The operators work Thai-first: speak slowly, lead with *where you are* — hotel name, road, district — and hand the phone to any Thai speaker nearby if you can. Hotel front desks make this call flawlessly; "call 1669 for me" is a complete sentence.

**1155**, the tourist police, answer in English around the clock and can conference-bridge you to the right service when you're not sure what you need. That's their whole job, and they're good at it.

## Chiang Mai's emergency rooms, with phones

Private-hospital ambulances also run 24 h and often arrive faster in town; call the hospital's main line and say "emergency."


| 24 h emergency room | Main line | From Tha Phae Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai | **052 089 888** | ~3.5 km |
| Chiang Mai Ram Hospital | **053 920 300** | ~1.9 km |
| Maharaj Nakorn (Suan Dok) | **053 936 150** | ~2.1 km |
| McCormick Hospital | **053 921 777** | ~2.1 km |
| Lanna Hospital | **052 134 777** | ~2.8 km |
| Rajavej Chiang Mai Hospital | **052 011 999** | ~2.6 km |
| Nakornping Hospital | **053 999 235** | ~7.7 km |
| Theppanya Hospital | **053 852 990** | ~3.2 km |

*Curated by residents, cross-checked against the household map, 2026-09-08. If a line changes, [tell us](/contact/) and it gets fixed the same week.*


The full picture of who's good at what — public vs private, billing, insurance — lives on [the hospital guide](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/).

## Six words of Thai that move help

| Say | Thai | Means |
|---|---|---|
| *chûai dûai!* | ช่วยด้วย | Help! |
| *rîak rót phá-yaa-baan* | เรียกรถพยาบาล | Call an ambulance |
| *rohng-phá-yaa-baan thîi glâi thîi-sùt* | โรงพยาบาลที่ใกล้ที่สุด | The nearest hospital |
| *jèp thîi nîi* | เจ็บที่นี่ | It hurts here |
| *pai rohng-phá-yaa-baan* | ไปโรงพยาบาล | Go to the hospital (to a driver) |
| *reo reo* | เร็ว ๆ | Quickly |

## The quiet preparation that pays

- **Put 1669 and your hotel's address in your phone tonight.** In Thai script too, if you can — screenshots of the hotel's LINE location pin work.
- **Carry your insurance card and one photo ID.** Private ERs move faster when the billing question answers itself; [[=Recourse|how you're protected]] explains the paperwork trail.
- **US veterans:** ER care abroad can be reimbursable under the VA Foreign Medical Program — [[=VA-FMP|the FMP page]] walks the claim.
- **Embassies come later.** Medical first, then your embassy's citizen services if you're admitted; they help with notification and records, not treatment.

## FAQ

### What is the emergency number in Thailand?
**1669** for medical emergencies and ambulances, nationwide and free. **191** is police, **199** is fire, **1155** is tourist police in English.

### Do Thai ambulances cost money?
The public 1669 service is free. Private hospital ambulances bill like the private hospitals they belong to — real but published numbers, usually settled with the ER bill.

### Will the 1669 operator speak English?
Assume Thai-first. Lead with your location, speak slowly, or have any Thai speaker — hotel desk, taxi driver, neighbor — place the call. 1155 (tourist police) bridges in English when you're stuck.

# Women's Health in Chiang Mai: Mapped, Phoned, and Priced
URL: https://defiant.to/articles/womens-health-chiang-mai/

Finding a gynecologist in a new country is a chore layered on top of something personal, and most of what the internet offers is a forum thread from 2019. Chiang Mai deserves better coverage than that: the city has a deep bench of OB-GYNs, hospital women's centers with modern screening equipment, university faculty, and the standing Thai custom that makes all of it approachable — walk-in clinics, posted prices, and no gatekeeping referral maze between you and a specialist.

The household mapped the whole landscape. Here it is.

## The map says


**258 women's-health facilities** are mapped across Chiang Mai in the household's dedicated dataset — OB-GYN clinics, hospital women's centers, fertility and screening services. The nearest to the old city:

| Facility | From Tha Phae Gate |
|---|---|
| **Klangya Thapae** (คลังยาท่าแพ) | ~0.1 km |
| **Dental 4U** | ~0.2 km |
| **Panu MD. Clinic** (ภานุการแพทย์) | ~0.2 km |
| **Moonmuang Pharmacy** (มูลเมืองเภสัช) | ~0.2 km |
| **PharmFriend** | ~0.3 km |
| **Mungkala Traditonal Chinese Medicine (acupuncture) Clinic** (มังคละโอสถ) | ~0.3 km |
| **Dr. Som** | ~0.3 km |
| **Tha Phae Clinic** (ท่าแพ คลีนิค) | ~0.4 km |

*From the household's Chiang Mai women's-health dataset, refreshed 2026-09-08. A missing clinic is a [fixable report](/contact/).*


## The three ways in

- **Hospital women's health centers** — the private hospitals on [the hospital guide](/articles/chiang-mai-hospitals/) all run dedicated centers: imaging and labs down the hall, English at the desk, appointments or walk-ins. The most comfortable first stop if you're new.
- **OB-GYN clinics** — Thailand's evening institution: hospital specialists (สูตินรีแพทย์, *sǔu-tì-ná-rii-phâet* — obstetrician-gynecologist) seeing patients at their own storefront clinics after hospital hours. Shorter waits, gentler prices, the same physician you'd meet at the hospital. The mapped rows above are full of them.
- **The university system** — Maharaj (Suan Dok) and Sriphat carry the deepest sub-specialty bench in the North: gynecologic oncology, urogynecology, fertility medicine. This is where complex things get answered.

## Asking for what you want is normal here

Three requests that are entirely ordinary in Thai clinics, stated in one sentence at the desk:

- **A female physician** — common, and commonly requested; hospital desks will tell you which sessions.
- **A chaperone in the room, or your partner with you** — routine either way.
- **English-language results** — ask at booking; every private facility above produces them.

Thai clinical style tends brisk and unembarrassed — screening questions arrive without ceremony, and it reads as efficiency, not judgment. Bring your history written down (dates, medications by generic name, prior results) and the visit runs beautifully.

## What routine care costs

*Indicative Chiang Mai private-sector ranges, August 2026 — posted or quoted flat, confirmed when you book.*

| Visit | Indicative |
|---|---|
| Specialist consult (clinic or hospital OPD) | **฿500–1,500** |
| Pelvic ultrasound | **฿800–2,500** |
| Cervical screening (with HPV testing tiers) | **฿1,000–3,500** |
| Mammogram + breast ultrasound | **฿2,500–6,000** |
| Annual women's checkup packages | **฿3,000–12,000** by tier |

Screening bundles ride the same package culture as [the general checkups](/articles/health-checkup-chiang-mai/) — named tiers, posted menus. For anything surgical or ongoing, get a quote in writing before anything books, which is [[=Concierge|the service]].


*Currency on this page: ฿100 ≈ $3.04 / €2.61 / £2.24 — Bank of Thailand mid rate, 2026-09-04. [Live board](https://motdang.net/finance.html) runs on [[=Home|the household's]] own feed.*


## Adjacent rooms on this site

Pelvic-floor physiotherapy has [[=Pelvic|its own page]] — one of Chiang Mai's genuinely underpriced specialties. Menopause care and HRT logistics live on [[=Estradiol|the estradiol page]]. And for care you're timing from abroad, [the return-trips guide](/articles/dtv-medical-runs/) covers labs-on-a-rhythm follow-up.

*Not medical advice — a map and a manners guide. Clinical decisions belong to you and your physicians.*

## FAQ

### How do I find an English-speaking gynecologist in Chiang Mai?
Start at a private hospital women's center — English at the desk is standard — or pick a mapped clinic above and ask when booking. Requesting a female, English-speaking physician is a normal one-sentence ask.

### How much does a gynecologist visit cost in Chiang Mai?
Indicative August 2026: ฿500–1,500 for the consult, with ultrasound ฿800–2,500 and screening bundles from about ฿1,000. Posted prices, no referral required.

### Do I need a referral to see a specialist?
No — Thailand runs on direct access. Walk into a hospital women's center or an OB-GYN's evening clinic and book the specialist directly.

### Can I get my results in English?
Yes — ask at booking rather than after. Private hospitals and established clinics produce English reports that travel well to doctors anywhere.
