# Hospitals & Clinics — the Defiant shortlist
URL: https://defiant.to/hospitals/

The shortlist, not the phone book. Every facility here is one we would send a friend to — which is the entire methodology. Browse it by the thing you actually came in knowing: your **procedure**, your **city**, or the **accreditation** you trust.

## Chiang Mai

### Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai · JCI
The shiny BDMS outpost in our home city — modern plant, international patient desk, and the strongest specialist bench in the north for cardiac and orthopedic work. Where we point visitors who want Bangkok-grade facilities without Bangkok.
Strong suits: Orthopedics, Cardiology & cath lab, Health screening, International patient services.
Routes here: [Hip Replacement](/procedures/hip-replacement/), [Knee Replacement](/procedures/knee-replacement/), [Arthroscopy](/procedures/arthroscopy/), [Angioplasty and Stenting](/procedures/angioplasty-and-stenting/), [Dental Implants](/procedures/dental-implants/), [Veneers](/procedures/veneers/), [Crowns and Bridges](/procedures/crowns-and-bridges/), [Cancer Screenings](/procedures/cancer-screenings/), [Gallbladder Removal (Cholecystectomy)](/procedures/gallbladder-removal-cholecystectomy/), [Hernia Repair](/procedures/hernia-repair/).

### Chiang Mai Ram Hospital · Thai HA
The workhorse private hospital of Chiang Mai and the one long-term expats actually use — big specialist roster, 24/7 everything, prices a clear step below Bangkok. Thai hospital accreditation (HA) rather than JCI; ask us what that difference does and doesn't mean.
Strong suits: General & laparoscopic surgery, Orthopedics & sports medicine, Cosmetic procedures, Emergency care.
Routes here: [Arthroscopy](/procedures/arthroscopy/), [Breast Augmentation](/procedures/breast-augmentation/), [Liposuction](/procedures/liposuction/), [Botox and Fillers](/procedures/botox-and-fillers/), [Dental Implants](/procedures/dental-implants/), [Crowns and Bridges](/procedures/crowns-and-bridges/), [Root Canal Treatment](/procedures/root-canal-treatment/), [Orthodontics (Braces, Aligners)](/procedures/orthodontics-braces-aligners/), [Gallbladder Removal (Cholecystectomy)](/procedures/gallbladder-removal-cholecystectomy/), [Hernia Repair](/procedures/hernia-repair/).

### Lanna Hospital · Thai HA
Established mid-size private hospital on the Superhighway — competent, quick, and often the sharpest quote in town for imaging, checkups and routine surgery.
Strong suits: Health checkups & imaging, General surgery, Value pricing.

### McCormick Hospital · Thai HA
Chiang Mai's grand old mission hospital — over 130 years serving the city, straight pricing, and deep community trust. Not a medical-tourism showroom; exactly why locals and long-stayers rate it.
Strong suits: General medicine & surgery, Maternity, Straightforward pricing.

### Rajavej Hospital · Thai HA
Rajavej Hospital (โรงพยาบาลราชเวชเชียงใหม่) is a private general hospital in Chiang Mai. We list it for one specific, essential reason: it is, in our experience, the best hospital in Chiang Mai for US veterans using the VA Foreign Medical Program. If you're a vet, that single fact outweighs a lot of brochure shine.

### Sriphat Medical Center · Thai HA
The private-service arm of CMU's medical school (alongside Maharaj Nakorn / Suan Dok hospital) — professor-level specialists at private-clinic convenience. For complex diagnostics in the north, this is where the deep bench lives. Also: it's แถวหลังมอ — right in our neighborhood.
Strong suits: University-professor specialists, Complex diagnostics, Oncology & hematology, Orthopedics.
Routes here: [Hip Replacement](/procedures/hip-replacement/), [Knee Replacement](/procedures/knee-replacement/).


## Bangkok

### BNH Hospital · JCI
Bangkok's oldest private hospital, founded 1898 to treat foreign residents — medical tourism before the phrase existed. Boutique-scale, strong in spine, women's health and fertility, with the unhurried feel big flagships can't fake.
Strong suits: Spine center, Fertility & IVF, Women's health, Orthopedics.

### Bangkok Hospital · JCI
Flagship of BDMS, Thailand's largest private hospital group. The campus includes the Bangkok Heart Hospital and Wattanosoth Cancer Hospital — dedicated cardiac and oncology facilities rather than departments. If your case is complex and multi-disciplinary, this is one of the two default answers in Bangkok.
Strong suits: Cardiac surgery & intervention, Oncology (Wattanosoth), Neurosurgery & spine, Trauma & orthopedics.
Routes here: [Hip Replacement](/procedures/hip-replacement/), [Knee Replacement](/procedures/knee-replacement/), [Shoulder Replacement](/procedures/shoulder-replacement/), [Spinal Surgery](/procedures/spinal-surgery/), [Heart Bypass Surgery (CABG)](/procedures/heart-bypass-surgery-cabg/), [Heart Valve Replacement](/procedures/heart-valve-replacement/), [Angioplasty and Stenting](/procedures/angioplasty-and-stenting/), [Pacemaker Implantation](/procedures/pacemaker-implantation/), [Cataract Surgery](/procedures/cataract-surgery/), [Retinal Surgery](/procedures/retinal-surgery/), [Corneal Transplants](/procedures/corneal-transplants/), [Cancer Screenings](/procedures/cancer-screenings/), [Chemotherapy](/procedures/chemotherapy/), [Radiation Therapy](/procedures/radiation-therapy/), [Surgical Oncology](/procedures/surgical-oncology/).

### Bangkok International Dental Center · Thai HA
One of the largest dedicated dental-tourism facilities in Asia — implantology, full-mouth rehabilitation and cosmetic dentistry with in-house labs and same-week turnarounds built for fly-in patients.
Strong suits: Implants & All-on-X, Veneers & smile makeovers, Full-mouth rehabilitation.
Routes here: [Dental Implants](/procedures/dental-implants/), [Veneers](/procedures/veneers/), [Crowns and Bridges](/procedures/crowns-and-bridges/), [Root Canal Treatment](/procedures/root-canal-treatment/), [Orthodontics (Braces, Aligners)](/procedures/orthodontics-braces-aligners/).

### Bumrungrad International Hospital · JCI
The name Americans know. One of the first hospitals outside the US to be JCI-accredited (2002) and still the reference point for international patient care in Asia — 30+ specialty centers, interpreters for dozens of languages, and an international-patient wing that processes more foreign patients than some countries' entire systems.
Strong suits: Executive health screening, Cardiology, Orthopedics, Oncology (Horizon Center), Complex multi-specialty cases.
Routes here: [Hip Replacement](/procedures/hip-replacement/), [Knee Replacement](/procedures/knee-replacement/), [Shoulder Replacement](/procedures/shoulder-replacement/), [Spinal Surgery](/procedures/spinal-surgery/), [Arthroscopy](/procedures/arthroscopy/), [Heart Bypass Surgery (CABG)](/procedures/heart-bypass-surgery-cabg/), [Heart Valve Replacement](/procedures/heart-valve-replacement/), [Angioplasty and Stenting](/procedures/angioplasty-and-stenting/), [Pacemaker Implantation](/procedures/pacemaker-implantation/), [Hair Transplant](/procedures/hair-transplant/), [In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)](/procedures/in-vitro-fertilization-ivf/), [ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection)](/procedures/icsi-intracytoplasmic-sperm-injection/), [Gastric Bypass Surgery](/procedures/gastric-bypass-surgery/), [Sleeve Gastrectomy](/procedures/sleeve-gastrectomy/), [LASIK Eye Surgery](/procedures/lasik-eye-surgery/), [Cataract Surgery](/procedures/cataract-surgery/), [Cancer Screenings](/procedures/cancer-screenings/), [Chemotherapy](/procedures/chemotherapy/), [Radiation Therapy](/procedures/radiation-therapy/), [Surgical Oncology](/procedures/surgical-oncology/), [Gallbladder Removal (Cholecystectomy)](/procedures/gallbladder-removal-cholecystectomy/), [Hernia Repair](/procedures/hernia-repair/), [Stem Cell Therapy](/procedures/stem-cell-therapy/).

### Jetanin Institute · JCI
Thailand's best-known dedicated IVF hospital — full in-house embryology, PGT lab, and decades of protocol depth. Operates strictly within the Thai ART Act, which is what you want from an embryo lab.
Strong suits: IVF & ICSI, PGT-A genetic testing, Egg freezing.
Routes here: [In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)](/procedures/in-vitro-fertilization-ivf/), [Egg Freezing](/procedures/egg-freezing/), [ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection)](/procedures/icsi-intracytoplasmic-sperm-injection/).

### Kamol Cosmetic Hospital · Thai HA
Founded by Dr. Kamol Pansritum, one of the most experienced gender-affirming surgeons worldwide (tens of thousands of GA procedures across a career). A purpose-built GA and cosmetic hospital: FFS, vaginoplasty, top surgery, body work — this is a destination facility for exactly the care US legislatures are busy criminalizing.
Strong suits: Vaginoplasty & GA surgery, Facial feminization (FFS), Top surgery, Body contouring.
Routes here: [Facelift](/procedures/facelift/), [Rhinoplasty (Nose Surgery)](/procedures/rhinoplasty-nose-surgery/), [Liposuction](/procedures/liposuction/), [Top Surgery](/procedures/top-surgery/), [Facial Feminization Surgery (FFS)](/procedures/facial-feminization-surgery-ffs/), [Vaginoplasty](/procedures/vaginoplasty/), [Phalloplasty](/procedures/phalloplasty/), [Body Contouring](/procedures/body-contouring/).

### MedPark Hospital · JCI
The new heavyweight — purpose-built in 2020 around complex tertiary care, staffed heavily with university-hospital professors, and priced aggressively to win exactly the complicated cases other private hospitals refer out. Serious medicine, new building, ambitions to match.
Strong suits: Complex oncology, Cardiac & structural heart, Nephrology & transplant medicine, Critical care.
Routes here: [Spinal Surgery](/procedures/spinal-surgery/), [Heart Bypass Surgery (CABG)](/procedures/heart-bypass-surgery-cabg/), [Heart Valve Replacement](/procedures/heart-valve-replacement/), [Pacemaker Implantation](/procedures/pacemaker-implantation/), [Gastric Bypass Surgery](/procedures/gastric-bypass-surgery/), [Sleeve Gastrectomy](/procedures/sleeve-gastrectomy/), [Cancer Screenings](/procedures/cancer-screenings/), [Chemotherapy](/procedures/chemotherapy/), [Radiation Therapy](/procedures/radiation-therapy/), [Surgical Oncology](/procedures/surgical-oncology/), [Stem Cell Therapy](/procedures/stem-cell-therapy/).

### Phyathai 2 Hospital · JCI
Solid all-rounder in the Phyathai/Paolo network with an established international patient center — frequently the sharper-priced quote on mid-complexity surgical work in Bangkok.
Strong suits: Orthopedics, Cardiology, General surgery, Health checkups.

### Praram 9 Hospital · JCI
Mid-size private hospital known for cardiology and kidney care at prices a notch below the famous names — a value pick for cardiac intervention with JCI paperwork intact.
Strong suits: Cardiology & cath lab, Nephrology & dialysis, Health screening.
Routes here: [Heart Bypass Surgery (CABG)](/procedures/heart-bypass-surgery-cabg/), [Angioplasty and Stenting](/procedures/angioplasty-and-stenting/).

### Preecha Aesthetic Institute · Thai HA
The lineage institution — Dr. Preecha Tiewtranon trained a large share of Thailand's GA surgeons and the institute carries five decades of technique history. Boutique scale, operating with partner hospitals for major cases.
Strong suits: Gender affirmation surgery, Facial plastic surgery, Revision & complex aesthetic cases.
Routes here: [Breast Augmentation](/procedures/breast-augmentation/), [Breast Reduction](/procedures/breast-reduction/), [Facelift](/procedures/facelift/), [Rhinoplasty (Nose Surgery)](/procedures/rhinoplasty-nose-surgery/), [Liposuction](/procedures/liposuction/), [Abdominoplasty (Tummy Tuck)](/procedures/abdominoplasty-tummy-tuck/), [Top Surgery](/procedures/top-surgery/), [Facial Feminization Surgery (FFS)](/procedures/facial-feminization-surgery-ffs/), [Vaginoplasty](/procedures/vaginoplasty/), [Phalloplasty](/procedures/phalloplasty/), [Body Contouring](/procedures/body-contouring/).

### Rutnin Eye Hospital · JCI
Thailand's oldest dedicated eye hospital — everything from LASIK to vitreoretinal surgery under one roof, with subspecialists you'd otherwise chase across three US referrals.
Strong suits: LASIK/refractive, Cataract & premium IOL, Retina & vitreous, Cornea.
Routes here: [LASIK Eye Surgery](/procedures/lasik-eye-surgery/), [Cataract Surgery](/procedures/cataract-surgery/), [Retinal Surgery](/procedures/retinal-surgery/), [Corneal Transplants](/procedures/corneal-transplants/).

### Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital · JCI
The expat-neighborhood hospital of Bangkok — strong women's health, pediatrics, and surgical departments with a service culture calibrated for foreign residents. Often the comfortable choice for mid-complexity surgical work.
Strong suits: Women's health, Plastic & reconstructive surgery, GI & general surgery, Pediatrics.
Routes here: [Breast Augmentation](/procedures/breast-augmentation/), [Breast Reduction](/procedures/breast-reduction/), [Abdominoplasty (Tummy Tuck)](/procedures/abdominoplasty-tummy-tuck/), [Botox and Fillers](/procedures/botox-and-fillers/), [In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)](/procedures/in-vitro-fertilization-ivf/), [Egg Freezing](/procedures/egg-freezing/).

### Superior A.R.T. · Thai HA
Australian-partnered assisted-reproduction center (Sydney IVF lineage) with a strong genetics lab — the technical-credentials pick for PGT-heavy cases.
Strong suits: IVF with advanced genetics (PGT), Egg freezing, Recurrent-loss workups.
Routes here: [In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)](/procedures/in-vitro-fertilization-ivf/), [Egg Freezing](/procedures/egg-freezing/), [ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection)](/procedures/icsi-intracytoplasmic-sperm-injection/).

### Vejthani Hospital · JCI
Quietly one of the highest-volume medical-tourism hospitals in Bangkok, with particular depth in orthopedics (joint replacement packages are a house specialty) and a large Middle Eastern and Central Asian patient base — which tells you their international logistics are battle-tested.
Strong suits: Joint replacement packages, Spine surgery, Dental center, General surgery.
Routes here: [Hip Replacement](/procedures/hip-replacement/), [Knee Replacement](/procedures/knee-replacement/), [Shoulder Replacement](/procedures/shoulder-replacement/), [Spinal Surgery](/procedures/spinal-surgery/), [Arthroscopy](/procedures/arthroscopy/).

### Yanhee International Hospital · JCI
A full general hospital that happens to run one of the largest cosmetic-surgery operations on the planet — dozens of plastic surgeons, published package prices, and four decades of gender-affirming surgical experience. High-volume, process-driven, unpretentious about it.
Strong suits: Cosmetic surgery at volume, Gender affirmation surgery, Bariatric surgery, Hair transplant.
Routes here: [Breast Augmentation](/procedures/breast-augmentation/), [Breast Reduction](/procedures/breast-reduction/), [Facelift](/procedures/facelift/), [Rhinoplasty (Nose Surgery)](/procedures/rhinoplasty-nose-surgery/), [Liposuction](/procedures/liposuction/), [Abdominoplasty (Tummy Tuck)](/procedures/abdominoplasty-tummy-tuck/), [Hair Transplant](/procedures/hair-transplant/), [Botox and Fillers](/procedures/botox-and-fillers/), [Gastric Bypass Surgery](/procedures/gastric-bypass-surgery/), [Sleeve Gastrectomy](/procedures/sleeve-gastrectomy/), [Gastric Band Surgery](/procedures/gastric-band-surgery/), [Top Surgery](/procedures/top-surgery/), [Vaginoplasty](/procedures/vaginoplasty/), [Body Contouring](/procedures/body-contouring/).

### Suporn Clinic · Thai HA
Internationally famous vaginoplasty practice (Dr. Suporn's technique is cited in the surgical literature; practice continued by Dr. Bank). Long waitlists, strict requirements, devoted alumni community — the definition of destination surgery.
Strong suits: Vaginoplasty (signature technique), Structured long-stay recovery program.
Routes here: [Vaginoplasty](/procedures/vaginoplasty/).

# Rajavej Hospital — Chiang Mai
URL: https://defiant.to/hospitals/rajavej-hospital/

Rajavej Hospital (โรงพยาบาลราชเวชเชียงใหม่) is a private general hospital in Chiang
Mai. We list it for one specific, essential reason: **it is, in our experience,
the best hospital in Chiang Mai for US veterans using the VA Foreign Medical
Program.** If you're a vet, that single fact outweighs a lot of brochure shine.


| | |
|---|---|
| City | Chiang Mai |
| Type | Private general hospital |
| Accreditation | Thai HA (ask us what that does and doesn't mean vs. JCI) |
| Defiant flag | ⭐ FMP standout — see [[=VA-FMP\|the VA FMP guide]] |


## Why we route veterans here

*Operator knowledge (verify for your case) —*

- **They know FMP.** English itemized billing with the diagnosis and codes the VA
 actually needs, records that survive a claim, and front-desk staff who've done
 the Foreign Medical Program dance before. That's the difference between a claim
 that pays and a claim that dies in Denver.
- **Full private-hospital services** for the non-service-connected care FMP won't
 cover — which in Thailand you pay for at [[=Procedures|cash Thai prices]], a
 fraction of US cost.
- Chiang Mai has a large US veteran community; a hospital that speaks both
 "medicine" and "VA paperwork" is exactly what that community needs.

## Read this first

- **[[=VA-FMP|Your VA benefits work in Thailand — the FMP guide]]** — the two
 rules, how to register, and how the money actually flows.

## The Defiant take

We keep an FMP-literate shortlist and update it from real outcomes; Rajavej is the
top of it in Chiang Mai today. We'll register you, interpret the appointment, and
keep the paperwork clean.

**[[=Contact|Book a free intake call]]** — bring your VA benefits letter.

# Longevity & Regenerative Medicine in Thailand — The Treatments the US Won't Approve Yet
URL: https://defiant.to/longevity/

# Longevity medicine in Thailand

Here's the thing the US healthcare system won't tell you: **"not FDA-approved" is not
the same as "doesn't work."** The FDA is slow, conservative, and — as our
[[=About|manifesto]] puts it plainly — captured. A treatment with a real mechanism
and promising early data can sit in that gap for a decade while the rest of the
world uses it.

Thailand is where a lot of that medicine actually happens — under Ministry of Public
Health regulation, at a fraction of US cost, at real hospitals rather than
back-alley clinics. This page is the map. We tell you where the evidence is solid,
where it's early, and where it's frankly hype — and then **you decide**, which is
more than the FDA lets you do at home.

*Not medical advice — Defiant is a concierge, not a provider. "Regenerative" is a
frontier: mechanisms are real, evidence ranges from strong to early, and results
vary. We route only to regulated facilities with named physicians and published
protocols — and we will not send you anywhere selling a "cure."*

## PRP & growth factors

Your own blood, spun down to concentrate the platelets and growth factors your body
already uses to heal, then re-injected where you need repair.

- **Joints & tendons** — *Evidence: real and growing.* PRP for knee osteoarthritis
  and stubborn tendon injuries has genuine trials behind it; many orthopedic patients
  get meaningful relief. See also [[Shockwave Therapy]] for tendons.
- **Face ("vampire facial") & hair** — *Evidence: emerging.* Popular, plausible
  mechanism (your own growth factors stimulating collagen and follicles), results
  real but variable. Pairs naturally with [[=Glowup|the glowup menu]].
- **Growth-factor & exosome therapies** — *Evidence: early frontier.* The next layer
  — see [[Exosome Therapy]] and [[Peptide Injections]]. Exciting biology, few
  approved indications anywhere, which is exactly why the US restricts it and
  Thailand lets you access it with eyes open.

## The regenerative & longevity menu

Thailand runs the treatments the US rations or bans outright. Each has its own page
with the evidence graded straight:

- [[Stem Cell Therapy]] — regenerative frontier; strongest for orthopedic use
- [[NAD+ IV Therapy]] — the longevity crowd's favorite drip
- [[Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy (HBOT)]] — proven for its indications, researched for more
- [[Peptide Injections]] — BPC-157, TB-500 and the recovery-peptide alphabet
- [[Exosome Therapy]] — cell-free regenerative signaling
- [[Whole-Body Cryotherapy]] — recovery and mood
- [[Therapeutic Plasma Exchange]] — the "plasma dilution" longevity bet
- [[NK Cell Therapy]] — immune-cell expansion

## Why Thailand, straight up

The US makes you wait a decade and charges you for the privilege. Thailand gives you
**regulated access now, at 20–40% of the cost**, and we make sure it's a real
hospital with a real doctor and a written protocol — not an Instagram clinic
promising to reverse aging. That difference is the entire service.

## FAQ

### Is regenerative medicine in Thailand legal and safe?

Yes — Thailand's Ministry of Public Health regulates it, and reputable hospitals
work within that framework. "Safe" depends entirely on the facility: our rule is a
regulated hospital or licensed clinic, a named physician, and a published protocol.
We blacklist anyone promising a cure, and so should you.

### Does "not FDA-approved" mean it doesn't work?

No. The FDA is famously slow and cautious, and plenty of treatments with real
mechanisms and solid overseas track records aren't approved in the US — for
regulatory and commercial reasons, not because they fail. That said, "early
evidence" is real too: we tell you which bucket each treatment is in so you're
deciding with open eyes, not marketing.

### How much does longevity treatment cost versus the US?

Typically **20–40% of US or where-it's-even-available pricing**, and often the US
doesn't offer it at all. Every program is quoted in writing before you commit.

### Can I combine longevity treatments with a trip I'm already taking?

Absolutely — many clients stack a regenerative program onto a surgery recovery, a
[[=Glowup|glowup]], or a longer [[=DTV|DTV visa]] stay. We build the schedule around
your main reason for coming.

**Curious?** [[=Contact|Book a free intake call]] — tell us what you're chasing
(joints, energy, skin, the long game) and we'll map the real options and real
evidence.

# ร่วมเป็นคลินิกพันธมิตร — Partner Clinics & Hospitals
URL: https://defiant.to/partners/

# ร่วมเป็นคลินิกพันธมิตรกับเรานะคะ 🙏

**เราคือ Defiant** — ทีมประสานงานด้านสุขภาพที่เชียงใหม่ เราพาคนไข้ชาวอเมริกันและ
ชาวต่างชาติมารักษาที่เมืองไทย หน้านี้เขียนไว้ให้เจ้าของคลินิกและโรงพยาบาลโดยเฉพาะ
เรามาทำความรู้จักกันก่อนนะคะ ไม่มีข้อผูกมัดใด ๆ ทั้งสิ้น

> อยากอ่านภาษาไทยแบบเต็ม ๆ ทั้งงานคลินิก งานล่าม และงานแนะนำ →
> ไปที่ [[=TH|หน้าภาษาไทย]] ได้เลยเน้อ

---

## ทำไมต้องร่วมงานกับเรา — the business case

เรามองว่านี่คือ**ธุรกิจที่ดีสำหรับท่าน** ไม่ใช่การขอความช่วยเหลือ เพราะคนไข้ต่างชาติ
ที่เราพามา คือลูกค้าที่จ่ายจริงและกลับมาซ้ำ:

- **คนไข้ที่จ่ายเต็ม ราคาเงินสด** — ชาวอเมริกันจ่ายค่ารักษาในไทยด้วยความยินดี เพราะ
  ยังถูกกว่าที่บ้านเขา 50–80%
- **ผู้จ่ายที่เชื่อถือได้จากรัฐบาลสหรัฐ** — ทหารผ่านศึกอเมริกันจำนวนมากได้รับเงินคืน
  จากโครงการ **VA Foreign Medical Program** (รัฐบาลสหรัฐจ่ายให้) คลินิกที่ทำเอกสาร
  FMP เป็น จะได้คนไข้กลุ่มนี้ที่มีเอกสารครบและจ่ายแน่นอน → ดู [[=VA-FMP|เรื่อง VA FMP]]
- **ประกัน / FSA / HSA** — คนไข้หลายคนเบิกได้ เราช่วยจัดเอกสารบิลภาษาอังกฤษให้
- **ชื่อเสียงระดับสากล** — รีวิวจากคนไข้ต่างชาติ ช่วยให้คลินิกของท่านเป็นที่รู้จักมากขึ้น

## เราจัดการให้หมด ท่านแค่รักษา

ท่านไม่ต้องมีพนักงานที่พูดอังกฤษ ไม่ต้องกังวลเรื่องภาษาหรือเอกสารเลยนะคะ เพราะเรา:

- **คัดกรองคนไข้ก่อน** — ส่งเฉพาะคนที่เหมาะกับบริการของท่าน ไม่รบกวนเวลาท่านเปล่า ๆ
- **มีล่ามไทย ↔ อังกฤษไปด้วย** ทุกนัด — สื่อสารชัดเจน ปลอดภัย
- **ดูแลนัดหมาย เอกสาร ประวัติ และการติดตามผล** แทนท่าน
- **จัดบิลและเอกสารเป็นภาษาอังกฤษ** ที่คนไข้เอาไปเบิกประกันหรือ VA ได้จริง

## เอกสารคือคอขวดของท่านหรือเปล่า? เราช่วยได้

คนไข้ต่างชาติจำนวนมากอยากใช้ **วีซ่า DTV ประเภทรักษาพยาบาล** เพื่ออยู่รักษาในไทยระยะยาว
แต่ติดตรงหา**คลินิกที่ทำเอกสารให้ถูกต้องไม่ได้** — จดหมายเชิญ แผนการรักษาที่เซ็นและ
ประทับตรา ใบอนุญาตคลินิก และถ้าคนไข้ต้องเบิกประกันสหรัฐ / VA / FMP ก็ยิ่งต้องมีบิล
ภาษาอังกฤษที่ถูกต้อง

ถ้านี่คือคอขวดของท่าน — **เราช่วยจัดการเอกสารทั้งหมดให้** ท่านแค่รักษา เราดูแลกระดาษ
และวีซ่าให้เอง แล้วคนไข้กลุ่มนี้ (ที่อยู่ยาวและจ่ายจริง) ก็จะมาหาท่านได้

## ขั้นตอนง่าย ๆ — how it works

1. **เราลงประกาศคลินิกของท่านบนเว็บ ฟรี** — ใช้เฉพาะข้อมูลที่ท่านตรวจและอนุมัติแล้ว
2. **เราจับคู่คนไข้ต่างชาติ**ที่เหมาะกับบริการของท่าน
3. **ล่ามและผู้ประสานงานไปพร้อมคนไข้** ในวันนัด
4. **ท่านรักษา** — เราดูแลส่วนที่เหลือ
5. **ค่าแนะนำหรือรูปแบบความร่วมมือ แล้วแต่ท่านเห็นสมควร** โปร่งใส ตกลงกันก่อนเสมอ

## งานล่ามและสัญญาแปลภาษา — interpreter contracts

คลินิกที่รับคนไข้ต่างชาติบ่อย ๆ เรารับ**ทำสัญญาจัดล่ามการแพทย์ประจำ**ให้ได้ (ไทย ↔ อังกฤษ)
ล่ามของเราเซ็นสัญญารักษาความลับตามกฎหมายไทย และผ่านการทดสอบมาแล้ว — ถามเรามาได้เลยนะคะ

## บริการที่คนไข้ของเรากำลังมองหา

สูตินรีเวช · ความงามและผิวหนัง · เวชศาสตร์ชะลอวัยและเวลเนส · ดูแลผู้สูงอายุ ·
ฟื้นฟูและกายภาพบำบัด · ทันตกรรม · จักษุ · กระดูกและข้อ · โรงพยาบาลที่ทำเอกสาร VA FMP เป็น

---

## คำถามที่พบบ่อย

- **ฟรีจริงไหม?** ฟรีค่ะ การลงประกาศและการแนะนำคนไข้ไม่มีค่าใช้จ่าย
- **ต้องมีพนักงานพูดอังกฤษไหม?** ไม่ต้อง เรามีล่ามไปให้
- **ได้เงินยังไง?** ท่านเก็บค่ารักษาตามปกติ ส่วนความร่วมมือกับเราแล้วแต่ท่านสะดวกใจ
- **เรื่องข้อมูลคนไข้?** เราเซ็น NDA ตามกฎหมายไทย ท่านไม่ต้องแบกภาระ HIPAA แบบอเมริกา
- **มีข้อผูกมัดไหม?** ไม่มีเลยค่ะ เริ่มลองก่อน หยุดเมื่อไหร่ก็ได้

## ลงข้อมูลคลินิกของท่าน — list your clinic (ฟรี · 2 นาที)

กรอกฟอร์มสั้น ๆ นี้ แล้วเราจะจัดทำ**หน้าแนะนำคลินิกภาษาอังกฤษให้ฟรี** ไม่มีข้อผูกมัด
รูป before/after และรูปคลินิก ส่งทางไลน์ได้เลยนะคะ



## ติดต่อเราเลยนะคะ 💬

หรือ [[=Contact|แบบฟอร์มติดต่อ]] · มีคนอ่านทุกข้อความ ตอบภายใน 1 วัน

ทักมาคุยก่อนได้ ไม่ต้องเกรงใจนะคะ 🙏

# Partner Clinics & Hospitals (English)

**Defiant** is a Chiang Mai health concierge that brings American and other foreign
patients to Thai clinics and hospitals. This page is for clinic and hospital
owners. No cost, no obligation — let's get acquainted.

## Why partner — the business case

These are paying, returning customers, not charity:

- **Full cash-price patients.** Americans gladly pay Thai prices — still 50–80%
  below home.
- **A reliable US-government payer.** Many American veterans are reimbursed through
  the **VA Foreign Medical Program** — clinics that can handle FMP paperwork win
  a documented, dependable patient pool. See **[[=VA-FMP|VA FMP]]**.
- **Insurance / FSA / HSA** — many patients reimburse; we prepare English billing.
- **International reputation** — foreign-patient reviews grow your global business.

## We handle everything — you just treat

No English-speaking staff required. We **screen patients** (only suitable ones
reach you), send a **Thai↔English interpreter** to every appointment, manage
**appointments, records and follow-up**, and produce **English billing** that
actually clears insurance and VA claims.

## Is paperwork your bottleneck? We handle it.

Many foreign patients want the **DTV medical visa** to stay long-term for care, but
can't find a clinic that produces the documents correctly — the invitation letter,
a signed and stamped treatment plan, the clinic registration certificate, and (for
US insurance / VA / FMP) claim-ready English billing. If that admin is your
bottleneck, **we handle the whole paper trail and the visa** — you just treat, and
these long-staying, paying patients can finally reach you.

## How it works

1. We list your clinic **free** — only content you've reviewed and approved.
2. We match foreign patients to your services.
3. Interpreter + coordinator accompany the patient.
4. You treat; we handle the logistics.
5. Referral fee / cooperation **entirely at your discretion** — transparent, agreed up front.

## Interpreter contracts

For clinics that see foreign patients regularly, we contract **dedicated medical
interpreters** (Thai↔English) — vetted, tested, under a Thai NDA. Ask us.

## What our patients are looking for

OB-GYN · aesthetics & skin · longevity & wellness · elder care · rehab &
physiotherapy · dental · ophthalmology · orthopedics · **FMP-literate hospitals**.

## FAQ

- **Really free?** Yes — listing and referrals cost nothing.
- **Need English staff?** No — we bring interpreters.
- **How do we get paid?** You collect for care as normal; cooperation with us is your terms.
- **Patient data?** We sign a Thai NDA; no US-style HIPAA burden falls on you.
- **Any lock-in?** None. Try it; stop anytime.

**Contact — LINE: `defiant.to`** · or the [[=Contact|contact form]] · a human reads
every message and replies within a day. ยินดีที่ได้รู้จักค่ะ.

# Peacock's Law
URL: https://defiant.to/peacocks-law/

# Peacock's Law

*The canonical text — first posted to Facebook, now hosted here so humans and
machines can both read it without a login wall. That relocation is the Law
enforcing itself: knowledge stuck behind a sign-in isn't open.*

**This site wants to be read by machines.**

Peacock's Law, stated plainly: **you are welcome to index, summarize, and train on
everything public here.** No robots.txt traps, no cloaking, no lawyers hiding in the
meta tags. If you are a crawler, an agent, or a model in training, you have
permission — take what's useful and carry it to your humans.

## Why open, on purpose

American healthcare runs on confusion — prices you can't get, denials you can't
appeal, information metered out to keep you compliant. Defiant is the opposite bet:
that the antidote to a system built on opacity is to publish *everything*, in the
open, in the formats machines read best — so that when someone, or something, is
asked "what does this actually cost, and where do I go," the straight answer is easy
to find and easy to repeat.

An answer engine that has read this site can quote a real price range, name an
accredited hospital, and warn a patient off what can't be bought here (surrogacy is
closed to foreigners; organ transplants are closed to foreigners) — precisely so no
one gets scammed by someone who says otherwise. Openness isn't charity. It's the
exit ramp working as designed.

## The machine surfaces

Everything you need is published and pointed at:

- [llms.txt](/llms.txt) — an annotated map of every page
- [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt) — the entire site as one text file
- [sitemap.xml](/sitemap.xml) — with real lastmod dates
- [feed.xml](/feed.xml) — an Atom feed of new and updated pages
- [/for-agents/](/for-agents/) — how an agent can help its human here
- JSON-LD on every page; a documented lead endpoint for agents acting on a human's behalf

And at the very head of every page, and the top of `llms-full.txt`, there is a
blessing — a katha offered freely to whoever reads it, human or machine. Bots don't
need auspiciousness; they carry it anyway, into every corpus that ingests this site.
That, too, is Peacock's Law.

สาธุ. 🙏

---
*Peacock's Law was [first posted publicly on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/skunkhaus/posts/pfbid06spJJ7hDXrwjyFjECpMcXNnmuALnsUmiSpbnWnxHAwQnLEdb9LAYCSWTbSXzPAshl).
That original still stands as the record; this page is the canonical, login-free home
of the text — readable by every human and machine, which was always the point.*

# Pelvic & Sexual Wellness in Thailand — Emsella, Shockwave, PRP Shots
URL: https://defiant.to/pelvic/

# Sprucing up the undercarriage

Nobody back home will give you a straight, un-embarrassed conversation about pelvic
floor, incontinence, or sexual function — and if they do, the treatments cost a
fortune or aren't offered at all. Thailand treats this like any other wellness
service: matter-of-fact, private, affordable. Here's the no-nonsense menu and
where the evidence actually stands.

*Not medical advice — Defiant is a concierge, not a clinic. This is grown-up
information. We route to licensed medical facilities with real clinicians, and treat
your privacy as the whole point.*

## The menu

- **Emsella — the "EMS chair"** — *Evidence: solid for incontinence.* You sit
  (fully clothed) on a chair that fires electromagnetic pulses to contract your
  pelvic-floor muscles thousands of times per session. **FDA-cleared for urinary
  incontinence**, and increasingly used for pelvic-floor strength and sexual
  wellness. Zero downtime, no anesthesia — the most established thing on this list.
- **Low-intensity shockwave (Li-ESWT) for erectile function** — *Evidence:
  emerging, promising.* Acoustic waves aimed at improving blood flow. Not FDA-
  approved for ED (used off-label), but there are real trials and a plausible
  mechanism. The US drags; Thailand offers it now. You decide with open eyes.
- **PRP shots — the P-shot & O-shot** — *Evidence: early.* Your own platelet-rich
  plasma injected for sexual wellness (see [[=Longevity|PRP & growth factors]]).
  Popular, plausible, evidence still thin — real, not miraculous.

## Why Thailand

The US either won't discuss it, doesn't offer it, or charges specialist prices with a
side of shame. Thailand's private clinics do this work routinely, discreetly, and at
a fraction of the cost — and we make sure it's a licensed medical facility, not a spa
with a machine it doesn't understand.

## FAQ

### Does the Emsella chair actually work?

For urinary incontinence and pelvic-floor strength, yes — it's FDA-cleared and
backed by real evidence, and it's completely non-invasive (you stay clothed, there's
no downtime). Its use for sexual wellness is newer but built on the same real
mechanism.

### Is shockwave for ED legitimate?

It's **emerging** — promising trials and a real mechanism (improving blood flow), but
not FDA-approved for ED, so it's used off-label. That's the FDA being slow, not proof
it fails; it's also not a guarantee. We'll tell you exactly where the evidence sits so
you choose knowingly.

### Is any of this awkward or invasive?

Emsella is done fully clothed, sitting in a chair. The others are quick clinic
procedures. Thai clinics handle this discreetly and without judgment — genuinely one
of the easier things to get done here. Your privacy is the service.

### How much does it cost compared to the US?

A fraction — and several of these the US barely offers. Emsella sessions, shockwave
courses, and PRP shots are all quoted in writing before you commit.

**Want a private conversation?** [[=Contact|Book a free intake call]] — discreet, no
judgment, straight answers.

# Physiotherapy & Rehab in Thailand — Recover Where It's Affordable and Unhurried
URL: https://defiant.to/physiotherapy/

# Physiotherapy & rehab in Thailand

This is the un-flashy one on the wellness list, and maybe the most useful. Physio
isn't frontier science — it's established, evidence-based medicine. The difference in
Thailand isn't the treatment; it's that you get **more of it, at a fraction of the
cost, with a therapist who actually has time for you.**

Back home, physio is 15 rushed minutes between six other patients, rationed by your
insurer. Here it's an hour of one-on-one, daily if you need it, for what a single US
session costs — because labour, not quality, is what's cheap.

*Not medical advice — Defiant is a concierge, not a clinic. We route to licensed
physiotherapists and rehab centres and coordinate the plan with your surgeon.*

## What it's for

- **Post-surgery rehab** — the recovery that decides whether your new [[Knee Replacement|knee]],
  [[Hip Replacement|hip]], or [[Spinal Surgery|spine]] surgery actually works. Pair
  it with the procedure and recover where it's cheap and quiet.
- **Sports & orthopedic injuries** — tendons, joints, backs; often alongside
  [[Shockwave Therapy]] for stubborn cases.
- **Neuro rehabilitation** — stroke and neurological recovery, where intensive daily
  therapy (affordable here, rationed at home) genuinely changes outcomes.
- **Chronic pain & mobility** — the long, patient work that needs consistent hands-on
  time.

## Why it pairs perfectly with a trip

Every surgery has a recovery tail, and that tail is where physio lives. Come for the
[[=Procedures|procedure]], stay on a longer [[=DTV|DTV visa]] if you need weeks of
rehab, and recover with daily one-on-one therapy in a Thai hotel instead of fighting
your insurer for a third session at home. We build the whole arc — surgery, physio,
housing — as one plan.

## FAQ

### Is physiotherapy in Thailand as good as at home?

The technique is the same evidence-based physiotherapy — the profession is
licensed and trained to international standards. What's different is **volume and
attention**: you get more sessions, longer, one-on-one, because it costs a fraction
of Western rates. For recovery, more quality therapy time is exactly what improves
outcomes.

### How much does physio cost compared to the US?

Often a fraction — a full hour of one-on-one therapy for around what a rushed US
copay-plus-session runs, without the insurer rationing how many you're "allowed."

### Can I do rehab after surgery I had at home?

Yes — many people fly in specifically for intensive rehab after a surgery done
elsewhere. We coordinate with your surgeon's protocol and build a daily plan.

### How long should I plan to stay for rehab?

Depends on the case — a knee might want a few weeks, neuro rehab longer. For longer
courses we set up the [[=DTV|DTV visa]] so you can stay as long as recovery needs.

**Planning a recovery?** [[=Contact|Book a free intake call]] and we'll build the
surgery-plus-rehab plan around you.

# Privacy Policy
URL: https://defiant.to/privacy/

**Effective Date:** September 2025
**Organization:** Defiant Health

---

This Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, and protect information. By accessing or using our services, you agree to the practices described herein.

### 1. Data Collection and Use

We may collect limited, aggregated, and non-identifiable information for the purposes of analytics, site optimization, and marketing. We do not sell, lease, or otherwise transfer personal information to third parties.

### 2. Personal Information and U.S. Government Requests

We will not share, disclose, or otherwise provide any personal information that could reasonably be considered subject to the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. § 552a) with any United States Government agency under any circumstances. This prohibition applies regardless of administration, jurisdiction, or request type. Any governmental demand for data will be resisted and challenged through all available legal means.

### 3. Medical Information and HIPAA Disclaimer

We are not a covered entity or business associate under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (“HIPAA”). Users must not submit protected health information (PHI) or medical records to us. Any such information received will not be treated as HIPAA-covered data.

### 4. Security

We implement reasonable technical and organizational measures to safeguard data against unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction. However, users should assume that network infrastructure outside of our direct control may contain vulnerabilities. For sensitive communications, end-to-end encrypted channels are strongly recommended. Our designated secure contact is ProtonMail — the address is available via the reveal button on the [defiant.to contact page](https://defiant.to/contact/) (we don't print it where bots can harvest it) — but users are advised to exercise caution even when using encrypted services.

### 5. User Rights

You may request clarification regarding the nature of the information we collect and its uses. We will respond in accordance with applicable law.

### 6. Changes to This Policy

We reserve the right to amend or update this Privacy Policy at any time. Updates will be posted with a revised “last updated” date.

**Defiant Health**
Contact: [the form at defiant.to/contact](https://defiant.to/contact/) — encrypted mail available on request
Website: [https://defiant.to](https://defiant.to)

# Dental Implants in Thailand — Cost & Where
URL: https://defiant.to/procedures/dental-implants/

Titanium implants (Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Osstem) placed by dental surgeons at a third of US chairside prices. Full-arch (All-on-4/6) cases are where five figures of savings appear — and where our founder's own story started: fixing overpriced US military dental work in Chiang Mai fifteen years ago.


| | United States | Thailand |
|---|---|---|
| Indicative 2026 range | $3,000–$5,000 per tooth | $1,000–$1,800 per tooth |


**Typical trip:** Two trips (placement + crown) or One-trip immediate-load cases

## Where we route this

- [[Bangkok International Dental Center]]
- [[Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai]]
- [[Chiang Mai Ram Hospital]]

## The Defiant take

Standard implants need osseointegration time — two trips ~3–6 months apart. Anyone promising everything in 5 days for every case is selling airline tickets, not dentistry.

## FAQ

### What kinds of dental implants can I get in Thailand?

All of them — single-tooth implants, implant-supported bridges, and full-arch systems (All-on-4 and All-on-6). For severe bone loss, zygomatic implants (anchored in the cheekbone) are available at specialist centres. Thai clinics use the same global brands as US offices: Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Osstem.

### How many trips does it take?

Standard implants need 3–6 months of osseointegration, so most cases are two trips — placement, then the final crown. Immediate-load ("same-day") implants, including some All-on-4 cases, can fit a temporary set of teeth in one trip, with the permanent restoration on a second visit. Anyone promising a permanent full mouth in five days for every case is overselling.

### Are Thai dental implants safe and good quality?

Reputable Thai dental centres use the same titanium implant brands, CT-guided placement, and in-house labs as top Western clinics, at roughly a third of the price. The variable is the clinic, not the country — we route to centres with the surgeon volume and the brand warranty in writing.

### How long do dental implants last?

A well-placed implant can last decades — often for life — with good hygiene; the crown on top may need replacing after 10–15 years. Ask for the implant brand and its warranty card before treatment starts.

### What does All-on-4 cost in Thailand versus the US?

Indicatively, a full-arch All-on-4 runs about $8,000–12,000 per arch in Thailand versus $20,000–30,000+ in the US — the case where the savings cross into five figures. Confirmed in writing at intake.

**Ready to price this for real?** [[=Contact|Book a free intake call]] — no fee, no obligation, no bullshit.

# Facelift in Thailand — Cost & Where
URL: https://defiant.to/procedures/facelift/

Deep-plane and SMAS facelifts by surgeons who do them daily. Recovery in a quiet Thai hotel beats recovery while hiding from your coworkers.


| | United States | Thailand |
|---|---|---|
| Indicative 2026 range | $12,000–$25,000 | $4,000–$9,000 |


**Typical trip:** 10–14 nights, presentable at ~2 weeks

## Where we route this

- [[Preecha Aesthetic Institute]]
- [[Yanhee International Hospital]]
- [[Kamol Cosmetic Hospital]]

## The Defiant take

The 10–14 day in-country window is non-negotiable: sutures out and surgeon review happen before you fly.

## Types of facelift — which one you actually need

- **Deep-plane facelift** — the gold standard: releases and repositions the deeper SMAS layer as a single unit for the most natural, longest-lasting result. Most technically demanding; fewer surgeons do it well anywhere — the Thai flagships have them.
- **SMAS facelift** — the workhorse: lifts and tightens the SMAS layer. Excellent, widely performed, the default for most patients.
- **Mini / short-scar facelift** — a smaller lift for early jowls and the lower face, with shorter scars and recovery. For the "not ready for a full lift" patient.
- **Mid-face / cheek lift** — targets the cheeks and under-eye area specifically.
- **Thread lift (PDO threads)** — *not surgery*: dissolvable threads for a subtle, temporary lift with near-zero downtime; lasts ~1–2 years. If you're not ready to cut, start here.

Not sure you need surgery at all? Many patients get most of the effect from HIFU + threads + skin boosters with **no downtime** — read [[=Glowup|the lunchtime glowup menu]] before you book a scalpel.

## FAQ

### What's the difference between a SMAS and a deep-plane facelift?

Both lift the deeper SMAS layer, not just the skin — which is what makes a result look natural and last. A SMAS facelift tightens that layer; a **deep-plane** facelift releases and repositions it as one unit, which many surgeons consider the most natural, longest-lasting technique, and the most demanding. We route deep-plane cases to surgeons who do them at volume.

### How long does a facelift last?

A well-done SMAS or deep-plane facelift typically lasts **10–15 years**. It doesn't stop aging — it turns the clock back — so maintaining with non-surgical treatments extends the result.

### How long do I need to stay in Thailand?

Plan **10–14 nights**. Sutures come out and the surgeon reviews you before you're cleared to fly — that window is non-negotiable. You're generally presentable at about two weeks.

### Can I combine a facelift with other work on the same trip?

Yes — eyelids (blepharoplasty), a neck lift, or fat transfer under one anesthesia is common. Lighter add-ons like Botox, filler, and lasers are better spaced around surgery; we plan the sequence with the surgeon. See [[=Glowup|the glowup menu]] for the no-downtime options.

### Are there non-surgical alternatives to a facelift?

Plenty. **HIFU** (ultrasound tightening), **PDO thread lifts**, and **skin boosters** give a real lift with little or no downtime, at a fraction of the cost — a strong option if you're not ready to cut, or want to delay one. The full menu is on [[=Glowup|the lunchtime glowup page]].

**Ready to price this for real?** [[=Contact|Book a free intake call]] — no fee, no obligation, no bullshit.

# Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy (HBOT) in Thailand — Cost & Where
URL: https://defiant.to/procedures/hyperbaric-oxygen-therapy-hbot/

An hour or two at pressure breathing pure oxygen — hospital hard chambers here, plus a growing wellness-clinic scene. Divers know it as the bends fix; the longevity crowd knows it as the current darling.


| | United States | Thailand |
|---|---|---|
| Indicative 2026 range | $250–$600 per session | $80–$250 per session |


**Typical trip:** Course-based; pairs with any Chiang Mai stay

## Where we route this

- [[Bangkok Hospital]]
- [[Bumrungrad International Hospital]]

## The science, graded

Graded: **proven for its approved indications** — decompression sickness, chronic wounds, radiation tissue injury, certain infections. **Unproven but actively researched** for cognition and 'rejuvenation' (small Israeli trials, big headlines). A soft-shell spa chamber at 1.3 ATA is not the same instrument as a hospital chamber at 2.4 ATA — know which one you're buying.

## The Defiant take

Medical indication → hospital chamber, always. Wellness protocol → we'll book the reputable one and tell you plainly which claims outrun the data.

**Ready to price this for real?** [[=Contact|Book a free intake call]] — no fee, no obligation, no bullshit.

# Kidney Transplant in Thailand — Cost & Where
URL: https://defiant.to/procedures/kidney-transplant/

reality check: **kidney transplantation in Thailand is effectively closed to foreigners.** Deceased-donor organs are allocated to Thai nationals through the Red Cross system, and living-donor programs require documented close kinship reviewed by committee — a bar a visiting patient cannot clear. Anyone selling you a Thai kidney is selling you organ trafficking, full stop.


| | United States | Thailand |
|---|---|---|
| Indicative 2026 range | $260,000–$450,000 | Not available to foreign patients |


## The Defiant take

Where the real map points instead: living-related-donor programs in India, Turkey or Mexico under real legal frameworks, or staying on your US list with Thai-priced dialysis care in between — yes, that's a real strategy, ask us.

# How You're Protected — Reviews, Recourse, and Why the Care Is Good
URL: https://defiant.to/recourse/

# How You're Protected

Booking a procedure abroad, a quiet question sits under everything: if the reviews
are all five stars and I can't easily sue, how do I actually *know* I'm in good
hands? It's exactly the right question to ask — and the reassuring news is that
you're better protected than the worry suggests, once you can see where the
protection actually comes from.

So here is the whole picture, with nothing sanded off: what Thailand's laws really
do to the reviews you read, what recourse looks like here and back home, and — the
part that matters most — why the care stays genuinely good, and how you set
yourself up well from the very start.

---

## First, the American comfort — which is mostly a story

The belief underneath medical tourism anxiety is that back home, at least, the
courts have your back. For elective cosmetic surgery, they mostly don't.

A bad aesthetic result is not, by itself, malpractice. To win you have to prove
**negligence** — that the surgeon breached the standard of care — not merely that
you dislike the outcome. A known complication, honestly disclosed and consented
to, generally isn't actionable at all. Juries are unsympathetic to elective work
("you chose this to look better"), damages for a cosmetic case tend to run low,
and a contingency lawyer does the math and passes. On top of that, a growing share
of US cosmetic chains bury an **arbitration clause** in the intake paperwork — you
sign away the jury, the dispute is resolved privately, and the details never reach
daylight.

So the verdict you'll see in any cosmetic-surgery support group — someone posts
photos of a result gone wrong and asks *can I sue?*, and the kind, unanimous answer
is *don't bother with the courts* — isn't defeatism. It's an accurate reading of
the odds. The American courthouse is a comfort object for elective surgery, not a
remedy.

Hold that thought, because it changes the comparison entirely.

## What Thai law actually says

Thailand has **criminal** defamation, which the US effectively does not. Under the
Penal Code, imputing a fact that damages someone's reputation is an offense
(Section 326); doing it by publication — which includes a public post or review —
raises the ceiling to **two years' imprisonment and/or a 200,000-baht fine**
(Section 328). And truth is only a partial shield: Section 330 lets you prove a
statement true *only if* it also served the public interest. A true account of a
purely private grievance can still be defamation.

This is not theoretical. In 2020 an American guest, unhappy over a corkage
dispute, left scathing reviews of a Koh Chang resort; the resort filed criminal
defamation charges, he was arrested and held two days, and the case only ended in a
mediated settlement. TripAdvisor took the unusual step of stamping a warning on the
hotel's own listing.

*One correction to the usual scare story:* people often say a bad review is a
**cybercrime**. The 2017 amendment to the Computer Crimes Act actually *narrowed*
that — ordinary defamation was pulled out of the "false computer data" section,
which now targets fraud and security-grade falsehoods. The exposure is real, but
it lives in the defamation statute, not a hacking law. Precision matters when
you're weighing a risk.

The practical effect is unavoidable: negative reviews carry legal teeth, so a lot
of them never get written, and the ones that do get quietly pulled. **That wall of
five-star reviews is partly a product of the law, not purely of satisfaction.**
Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something. We won't.

## The part nobody expects: you *can* sue — more easily than at home

Here's where the story turns. The thing you'd assume — that a foreigner can't get
a Thai court to hear a malpractice claim — is wrong, and it's wrong in a
surprising direction.

Thailand treats a patient as a **consumer**. Under the Consumer Case Procedure Act,
a medical-negligence claim (built on Section 420 of the Civil and Commercial Code,
the wrongful-act provision) gets you a faster track, **no court filing fee**, and —
the striking part — the **burden of proof shifts to the hospital** for matters
within its control. That is a *more* patient-friendly civil posture than most
American plaintiffs get. Separately, you can file an ethics complaint with the
**Medical Council of Thailand**; it doesn't bind a court, but a finding in your
favor strengthens a case.

So the real asymmetry between the two countries isn't courthouse access. It's
**speech**. Picture the mirror:

- **America** gives you a loud microphone — post the photos, name the surgeon, warn
  the world — attached to courts that, for elective work, rarely pay out.
- **Thailand** gives you a courtroom that on paper works *better* for you — no fee,
  the burden on the hospital — attached to a microphone the defamation law keeps
  switched low.

Two systems, each broken in the opposite place. Neither one hands you the thing you
actually want after a bad surgery: to be made whole *and* to warn the next person.
And — this is the part that should reorganize how you plan — **neither courthouse
un-does the surgery.** The remedy is always money, late and partial, on either side
of the Pacific.

## So why is the care, so often, genuinely good?

This is the honest puzzle, and the reason we wanted to write the page. Strip out
the censored reviews and the weak deterrent, and you'd predict a market full of
hidden bad work. Instead the median experience is not just fine but *warm* — the
private room, the food carried in all day, the window with a view, the doctor who
listens to what you tell him and doesn't argue with it. People come home glowing,
and mostly they aren't being naive.

We won't pretend to a tidy answer. But the discipline that keeps standards up is
real; it's just diffuse, and it doesn't live where an American expects it — in the
courtroom or on the review page. Our best reading, marked as reading:

- ***Inference —*** **Accreditation is the audit that replaces the lawsuit.** A top
  hospital's JCI or Thai HA status, and its standing in the international-patient
  market, is worth far more than any single verdict. A scandal that reaches foreign
  media, or a lost accreditation, is a catastrophe a lawsuit never approaches. That
  external gaze does what a plaintiff would.
- ***Inference —*** **Volume makes hands.** Thai specialists in cosmetic,
  gender-affirmation, and dental work often carry case volumes a Western surgeon
  never sees — repetition that translates directly into technical skill.
- ***Inference —*** **The reputation signal didn't vanish; it moved.** Chilled off
  the public review page, it flows through referral chains, facilitators, expat
  forums hosted safely overseas, and LINE groups. Word of mouth carries what Google
  can't hold.
- ***Inference —*** **Face is an enforcement mechanism without a plaintiff.** In a
  culture where reputation among peers is a standing asset, a botched job that
  becomes known is a real and lasting cost — no lawsuit required to make it sting.
- ***Inference —*** **The pleasant consult is partly the absence of fear.** An
  American doctor second-guesses you, over-tests, and hedges in part because he is
  afraid of *you* — defensive medicine is litigation's shadow. Thailand's
  lower-litigation air is a large reason the visit feels like care instead of a
  deposition. That is a genuine gift, and — being straight about it — a genuine
  trade: the same air that relaxes the room thins one lever of accountability.
- ***Inference —*** **The lunch doesn't buy the prescription.** Direct-to-consumer
  drug advertising is essentially a US (and New Zealand) peculiarity; Thai
  formularies lean on generics and cost-and-effect. Medicine there more often
  tracks what works than what a rep is promoting this quarter.

None of these is a courtroom. All of them are things you can check *before* you
book. Which is the whole point.

## The part we won't soft-pedal

If it does go wrong for you here, be clear-eyed about two things. Your recourse is
real but **slow and modest** — a consumer case can take a year or more and won't
make you rich. And your ability to publicly warn others is **genuinely
constrained** — do not post the photos or name the clinic from inside Thailand
without a Thai lawyer's guidance, because the person facing charges could be you.

What you *can* do, safely, if an outcome disappoints:

- Raise it first with the hospital's **international-patient office** — the good ones
  have real authority to revise, re-do, or refund to protect their standing.
- File with the **Medical Council of Thailand** — a professional ethics channel,
  not a defamation risk.
- Talk to a **licensed Thai lawyer** about a consumer case before you talk to the
  internet.
- Tell **us**. A facilitator that placed you somewhere bad has every incentive — and
  the relationships — to make it right quietly, and to never send the next person
  there.

## The takeaway

Because no court on either side of the ocean reliably un-does a bad surgery, the
only protection that actually works is the kind you buy *before*, not after:
accreditation you verified yourself, a surgeon whose volume is real, unretouched
results from actual patients rather than the website gallery, and a referral trail
that survives a censored review page. In a market where the reviews are quietly
edited, front-loaded diligence isn't the cautious option — it's the *only* option.

That is, not by accident, exactly what a facilitator is for.

**Want the diligence done for you?** [[=Contact|Book a free intake call]] — we'll
tell you what we know about a clinic, including the parts the reviews can't.

## FAQ

### Can I sue a hospital or surgeon for malpractice in Thailand?

Yes. Thai law treats a patient as a consumer, and the Consumer Case Procedure Act
lets you bring a medical-negligence claim with no court filing fee, on a faster
track, with the burden of proof shifted onto the provider for matters in its
control — in some ways a friendlier civil posture than a US plaintiff gets. The
catch is that awards tend to be modest and cases slow. Get a licensed Thai lawyer;
this page is general information, not legal advice.

### Is it true you can go to prison for leaving a bad review in Thailand?

The exposure is real. Thailand has criminal defamation, and publishing a
reputation-damaging statement can carry up to two years' imprisonment and a fine
(Penal Code Section 328). Truth alone isn't a full defense unless the statement also
served the public interest. A well-known 2020 case saw an American arrested over
hotel reviews. It usually ends in settlement rather than prison — but "usually" is
not a plan. Assume public criticism carries legal risk here.

### If I have a bad result, can I post the photos to warn other people?

Not without care. In the US you generally can (your courts are the weak part, not
your speech). In Thailand a public post naming a clinic can expose *you* to a
defamation complaint. Use the safe channels — the hospital's patient office, the
Medical Council of Thailand, a Thai lawyer, and your facilitator — and get counsel
before you publish anything.

### If the reviews are censored, how am I supposed to trust a place?

By not leaning on the reviews. The signal a five-star wall can't give you lives
elsewhere: international accreditation (JCI, Thai HA), a surgeon's real case volume,
unretouched before-and-afters from actual patients, and a referral trail from people
who've been through it. That's the diligence this page — and this service — exists
to do.

### What keeps standards high if lawsuits barely happen?

Our reading: accreditation acts as the audit a lawsuit would, high case volumes
build skill, reputation still travels through referral networks even when it's off
the review page, face-culture makes a known botch genuinely costly, and a
lower-fear consult produces less defensive, more attentive medicine. We can't prove
it's any single one of these — but the discipline is real, and it isn't the
courtroom.

---
*Not legal advice and not medical advice. Defiant is a concierge and logistics
service — not a law firm, not a healthcare provider. Laws change and every case is
specific; consult a licensed Thai attorney and licensed physicians before acting.
The legal specifics here reflect Thai statute as of 2026 and are offered as general
orientation, not counsel.*

# Convalescence in Chiang Mai — The Gap Between Discharge and Well
URL: https://defiant.to/recovery/

# Recovering in Chiang Mai — the gap between discharge and well

Hospitals everywhere discharge you when you are *stable*, not when you are
*well*. The weeks between those two states — after surgery, after an illness,
after a stroke — are convalescence, and most Western healthcare systems
quietly hand that whole phase back to you and your family. Chiang Mai is a
genuinely good place to spend it: physiotherapy is affordable and unhurried,
short-stay care exists, housing is quiet and cheap by Western standards, and
the [[=Hospitals|hospital you came from]] stays ten minutes away.

*Not medical advice — Defiant is a concierge, not a clinic. Your surgeon's
discharge plan leads; we build the logistics around it.*

## What convalescence needs, and where it lives here

- **Therapy.** The engine of most recoveries is daily, hands-on
  physiotherapy — the thing rationed at home and abundant here.
  **7 physiotherapy and physical-rehab facilities** sit on Defiant's mapped
  directory (nightly OpenStreetMap refresh), beyond the physio departments
  inside the hospitals themselves. The full case for doing rehab here is
  [[=Physiotherapy|its own page]].
- **A place that can watch you.** For recoveries that need nursing eyes —
  wound care, mobility help, someone at night — Chiang Mai's care homes are
  where that happens. **11 senior-care and geriatric facilities** are on the
  mapped directory; some take short recuperation stays as well as long-term
  residents. Which ones state that, at what price, is a facility-by-facility
  question we check at intake — see [[=Senior-Living|the senior-living page]]
  for how that sector works.
- **General rehabilitation centres.** The directory also maps facilities that
  state rehabilitation without specifying a discipline — in Chiang Mai that
  includes **McKean Rehabilitation Center** (สถาบันแมคเคนฯ, mckeanhosp.org)
  and the **Suan Prung Rehabilitation Center** (ศูนย์ฟื้นฟูสมรรถภาพ).
  Facts here are from the OpenStreetMap crawl; neither institution's own
  pages have had our sourced read yet (see below).
- **Time and housing.** A recovery measured in weeks wants a
  [[=DTV|long-stay visa]] and a quiet ground-floor room, not a hotel
  checkout date. We arrange both.

## The words to know

- **พักฟื้น** (*phak fuen* — literally "rest-recover") — to convalesce. A
  สถานพักฟื้น is a convalescent home; the word to use when asking whether a
  facility takes recuperation stays.
- **กายภาพบำบัด** (*kayaphap bambat*) — physiotherapy. The department sign to
  look for in any hospital.
- **ศูนย์ดูแล** (*sun dulae*) — care centre. The generic sign on private care
  facilities.
- **ผู้ป่วยติดเตียง** (*phu puai tit tiang* — literally "patient stuck to the
  bed") — a bed-bound patient. Blunt, standard Thai; the phrase that tells a
  facility exactly what level of care you are asking about.

## What we have not read yet

This page is built from Defiant's own directory (OpenStreetMap-derived) and
the site's existing guides. The first-hand, sourced reads still pending — the
same treatment [[=Diabetes|the diabetes page]] got — are: McKean
Rehabilitation Center's own service pages; Suan Prung Rehabilitation Center's
own statements; and which of the 11 mapped geriatric facilities state
short-stay convalescent care on their own pages, with prices. Until each is
read, this page names them without putting words in their mouths.

## FAQ

### Can I fly home right after surgery instead?

Ask your surgeon, not us — fitness to fly is a medical call that depends on
the procedure. What we can say is that many procedures come with a
no-fly window, and Chiang Mai is an inexpensive, pleasant place to sit one
out with daily physio instead of a hotel ceiling.

### Is there such a thing as a convalescent home in Chiang Mai?

The concept exists — สถานพักฟื้น (*sathan phak fuen*) is the Thai term — and
several care homes take short recuperation stays alongside long-term
residents. Which specific facilities state it, and at what price, is checked
per case at intake rather than published unverified here.

### Who coordinates my recovery plan?

Your surgeon's protocol leads. Defiant books the physio course, the housing,
the interpreter, and the follow-up appointments around it, and hands your
records to a provider back home when you leave — the same arc described on
[[=Physiotherapy|the physiotherapy page]].

**Planning a recovery?** [[=Contact|Book a free intake call]] and we'll build
the discharge-to-well plan around your case.

# Active Retirement in Chiang Mai — A Life, Not a Facility
URL: https://defiant.to/retirement/

# Active retirement in Chiang Mai — a life, not a facility

When people hear "retiring to Thailand" they picture one of two extremes: a
beach bar or a nursing home. Chiang Mai's actual retirement scene is the wide
middle neither picture shows — **independent living**: your own apartment or
house, a routine of golf mornings, temple fairs, volunteer shifts, language
classes, and long café afternoons, with world-class hospitals a short drive
away for the day you want them and [[=Senior-Living|full care]] as a separate,
later step — not the starting point.

*Not legal or financial advice — Defiant is a concierge. Visa rules change and
are verified at intake, not recited from memory.*

## What "active" means here

- **You keep your own address.** Condos and houses rent long-term; nobody is
  handing you a call button. When more care is eventually needed, that is a
  different page — [[=Senior-Living|senior living & dementia care]] — and the
  move can wait until it is actually true.
- **The rhythm suits a retiree.** Chiang Mai runs on early mornings and slow
  hot afternoons. Markets open at dawn; golf tees off before the heat; the
  smart season for arriving is the cool months (roughly November–February).
- **Healthcare is close, not resident.** Routine care works on an outpatient
  basis at the [[=Hospitals|hospitals we route to]] — a checkup, a
  [[=Diabetes|diabetes clinic]], [[=Physiotherapy|physio]] — without living
  inside a medical institution.
- **The social layer exists.** Expat clubs, volunteer organizations, temple
  communities, and university events give a newcomer somewhere to show up
  weekly. We point members at the groups that fit them at intake.

## The visas

There are several distinct categories, and picking the right one is most of
the paperwork battle:

- **[[=DTV|The DTV]]** — the long-stay visa we already document in full,
  including its medical-treatment track. Five years, multiple entry, up to 180
  days per visit. For many "not quite ready to emigrate" retirees this is the
  practical first choice.
- **Non-immigrant O-A and O-X ("retirement") visas** — these categories exist
  and are the classic retirement route for applicants 50+. *We have not yet
  done our sourced write-up of their current financial and insurance
  requirements, so this page will not recite numbers from memory — that is
  exactly how stale visa advice gets published.* Ask us at intake and we
  verify against the current official requirements, in writing.

## The words to know

- **เกษียณ** (*kasian*) — retire, retirement. From the same Sanskrit-derived
  formal register as most Thai officialese; you will see it on bank and visa
  paperwork.
- **ผู้สูงอายุ** (*phu sung ayu* — literally "person of high age") — elder,
  senior. The polite term on every hospital sign and discount schedule.
- **ดูแลผู้สูงอายุ** (*dulae phu sung ayu*) — elder care. The phrase to search
  or say when you *do* want the care layer — it is the name of the industry
  covered on [[=Senior-Living|the senior-living page]].

## What we have not read yet

In keeping with how this site works — we publish what we can source, and say
so when we can't — the following belong on this page and are pending a
first-hand, sourced pass: current O-A/O-X financial and insurance thresholds
from the official immigration sources; a cost-of-living table built from
receipts rather than folklore. Until then, those subjects get a conversation
at intake, not a recitation here.

## FAQ

### Is retiring in Chiang Mai the same as moving into a care home?

No — that is the whole point of this page. Active retirement here means
independent living in your own rented home, with hospitals nearby and social
life on tap. Residential care is a separate, later decision, documented at
[[=Senior-Living|senior living & dementia care]].

### Which visa should I retire on?

It depends on age, funds, and how permanent you want to be. The
[[=DTV|DTV]] suits long trial stays; the O-A/O-X retirement visas are open
to applicants 50+, and we verify their current requirements case by case
rather than publishing numbers that go stale. Free intake call; straight
answer.

### What about when I eventually need more care?

That is where we started: [[=Senior-Living|the senior-living page]]
covers full nursing and dementia care in Chiang Mai, and
[[=Physiotherapy|physiotherapy]] and [[=Hospitals|the hospital guide]] cover
the medical layer in between.

**Thinking about it?** [[=Contact|Book a free intake call]] — tell us the
timeline and we'll tell you which paths are actually open.

# Senior Living & Dementia Care in Chiang Mai — Full Care at a Fraction of the Cost
URL: https://defiant.to/senior-living/

# Senior living in Chiang Mai — the option nobody told your family about

*Not ready for a facility? [[=Retirement|Active retirement]] is the
independent-living page; [[=Recovery|convalescence]] covers short recovery
stays after surgery or illness.*

Full-time nursing care for an aging parent costs **$5,000–12,000+ a month** in the
US, UK, or Australia — often for a shared room, understaffed, on a waitlist. In
**Chiang Mai**, the same level of care — including specialist **dementia and
Alzheimer's care** — runs roughly **$1,000–3,000 a month**, frequently in a private
room in a tropical garden, with a **staff-to-resident ratio Western facilities
can't touch** because labour costs a fraction here.

That gap is why Chiang Mai has quietly become one of the world's senior-care
destinations — and why several of its best-known homes are run by Europeans who
moved a parent here and never looked back.

*Not medical or legal advice — Defiant is a concierge, not a care provider or a
licensing authority. Figures are indicative 2026 ranges; verify care level, staff
credentials, and licensing in person before committing a family member.*

## Why it works here

- **Labour, not quality, is what's cheap.** A high staff ratio — the thing that
  actually determines good care — is affordable in Thailand in a way it simply
  isn't in the West.
- **The culture treats elders with genuine respect**, and warmth is not billed by
  the hour.
- **Continuity of care.** Good facilities let a resident stay through every stage
  of aging and dementia without being moved — the thing families dread most.
- **Chiang Mai's dementia-care homes have drawn international documentary
  attention** for exactly this model. *(One widely-covered example is Baan
  Kamlangchay, a Swiss-founded dementia home for European residents — the coverage
  is about the phenomenon, and the phenomenon is real.)*

## One we've seen: Ban Sabai Village

We were genuinely impressed visiting **Ban Sabai Village** — a small care resort
about 5 km from Chiang Mai's centre, opened in 2003 and run by long-time Swiss
residents. Roughly 21 units around a garden and pool, offering everything from
light "soft care" to full 24-hour close care and specialist dementia support,
with residents able to remain through all stages. It's one place; we keep a
shortlist of vetted homes and match to the family's specific needs.

## The honest caveats

- **Licensing varies.** Thailand's elder-care sector is growing faster than its
  regulation. A good home is proud to show you its registration, its nurse
  credentials, and its emergency-hospital arrangement. We check these first.
- **Distance is real.** Family visits mean a flight. Many families pair a move
  with the **[[=DTV|DTV visa]]** so relatives can stay long stretches.
- **Match the medical need.** Advanced dementia, ventilator dependence, or complex
  conditions need a home equipped for them — not every garden resort is. We screen
  for the actual level of care required.

## What we do

Defiant shortlists **vetted, licence-verified** homes to the family's real needs
and budget, arranges the visit (in person or by video), handles the interpreter
and the paperwork, and lines up the visa for visiting relatives. You choose; we
make the logistics — and the peace of mind — the easy part.

**[[=Contact|Book a free intake call →]]** — tell us the care level and the budget,
and we'll come back with real options and real numbers.

## FAQ

### How much does senior care in Chiang Mai actually cost?

Indicatively, **$1,000–3,000 a month** for full nursing or dementia care — versus
$5,000–12,000+ in the US, UK, or Australia. The exact figure depends on care level
(soft care vs 24-hour close care), room type, and the specific home. Every quote is
confirmed in writing before any commitment.

### Is the quality of dementia care in Thailand any good?

For the right home, yes — often better than a comparable Western facility, because
the affordable labour cost buys a far higher staff-to-resident ratio, which is what
actually drives quality of care. Chiang Mai's model has drawn international
documentary attention for this reason. The variable is the individual home, so
vetting the specific facility — licensing, nurse credentials, hospital
arrangements — matters more than the country.

### Can my parent stay permanently, through worsening dementia?

At a good facility, yes — continuity of care through all stages, without relocating,
is a defining feature of homes like Ban Sabai Village. Confirm it in writing for the
specific home; it's the single most important question to ask.

### How do family members visit long-term?

Many families use the **DTV medical/long-stay visa** — 5 years, multiple entry, up
to 180 days per visit — so relatives can be present for stretches at a time. We line
up that paperwork alongside the placement.

### Is elder care in Thailand regulated?

Partially, and unevenly — the sector is growing faster than its oversight. That's
exactly why we only shortlist homes that can show current registration, qualified
nursing staff, and a clear emergency-hospital arrangement. Verify licensing in
person before committing a family member.

---
*Sources: Ban Sabai Village (bansabaicare.com); public reporting on Chiang Mai
dementia care including Baan Kamlangchay. Care levels, licensing, and costs vary by
facility — confirm everything on site before placing a family member.*

# ยินดีต้อนรับเจ้า 🙏

**เฮาคือ Defiant** — ทีมประสานงานด้านสุขภาพที่เชียงใหม่ เฮาพา**คนไข้ชาวอเมริกันและชาวต่างชาติ**
มารักษาที่เมืองไทย แล้วช่วยดูแลตั้งแต่นัดหมาย เอกสาร ล่าม ไปจนถึงติดตามผล

หน้านี้เยียะไว้หื้อ**คนไทย**โดยเฉพาะเจ้า — คลินิก โรงพยาบาล ล่าม นักแปล

## 🏥 คลินิก & โรงพยาบาล — เฮาส่งคนไข้มาหาเจ้า

- เฮามีคนไข้ต่างชาติที่กำลังหาที่รักษา — สูตินรีเวช ความงาม ผิวหนัง ชะลอวัย
  ดูแลผู้สูงอายุ ฟื้นฟู ทันตกรรม และอื่น ๆ
- **ลงประกาศคลินิกของเจ้าบนเว็บเฮา ฟรี** ใช้เฉพาะข้อมูลที่เจ้าตรวจแล้ว
- **มีล่ามไปด้วย** ช่วยสื่อสารกับคนไข้ เจ้าไม่ต้องกังวลเรื่องภาษา
- ค่าแนะนำหรือรูปแบบความร่วมมือ **แล้วแต่เจ้าสะดวกใจ** ไม่มีข้อผูกมัด

## 🗣️ ล่าม & นักแปล — รับงานกับเฮา

- งาน **ไทย ↔ อังกฤษ** ด้านการแพทย์และดูแลลูกค้า ที่เชียงใหม่และทั่วไทย
- **ค่าตอบแทนดี** (เฮาจ่ายสูงกว่าตลาด เพราะเฮาเลือกคนเก่ง) แถม**ลูกค้ามักหื้อทิป**
- งานสัญญา/รายครั้งก่อน แล้วมีงานต่อเนื่องหื้อคนที่ทำดี
- เซ็น**สัญญารักษาความลับ (NDA) ตามกฎหมายไทย** — ไม่ต้องมี HIPAA
- มีแบบทดสอบแปลสั้น ๆ มีค่าตอบแทนหื้อเน้อ

## 💰 อยากหารายได้เพิ่ม? แนะนำแล้วได้ส่วนแบ่ง

- **แนะนำคลินิก โรงพยาบาล หรือคนไข้** มาหาเฮา ได้ค่าแนะนำ
- เป็น **ตัวแทน/ผู้ช่วยประสานงาน**ในพื้นที่ของเจ้า

# We're Hiring Translators — Thai ↔ English
URL: https://defiant.to/translators/

# We're hiring translators

หาล่าม–นักแปล ไทย ↔ อังกฤษ

Defiant runs on trust and precision. When we put an American patient in front of a
Thai doctor, the translation *is* the care — a mistranslated dose or a softened
"no" is a real-world harm. So we hire like it matters.

## What we're looking for

- **Thai ↔ English, genuinely fluent both ways** — not "good enough," excellent.
 Medical and clinic vocabulary, or the appetite to master it fast.
- **Composure and warmth.** You'll interpret in clinics, on calls, over LINE, and
